abstract: ArXiv:2610.33246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum simulations on noisy hardware are often designed as if the machine were ideal, with device limitations considered only after the basis and measurement plan have been chosen. We instead use information about the physical problem and the device at an earlier stage, to decide which states and evolution times should form a compact simulation basis. Because the target problem remains unchanged, the method adapts only the representation used to solve it. Tests on many-body and molecular models show that this approach can reveal useful directions that ordinary time evolution misses, while also exposing an important limitation: some of these directions can become too similar to estimate reliably. Realistic device data further show that hardware response can change the preferred states and evolution times before execution. Across seven acquisition days, a four-qubit experiment shows a median 54\% reduction in projected-energy error from problem-informed time choices relative to uniform sampling under matched hardware conditions. These results provide a proof of principle for simulation-basis design as a practical interface between quantum algorithms and the hardware that executes them.
tldr: A hardware-aware co-design scheme that chooses simulation basis states and evolution times from both the target many-body/molecular problem and measured device noise, rather than fixing the algorithm first.
motivation: Quantum simulation protocols are typically designed under ideal-machine assumptions, with device limitations patched in only after the ansatz, basis, and measurement schedule are fixed, which wastes limited coherent resources on noisy hardware.
method: The authors use information about the physical Hamiltonian and device response at an early stage to select a compact set of states and evolution times forming the trial space, then benchmark this problem-informed sampling against uniform time sampling on many-body and molecular models, including a four-qubit experiment re-characterized over seven acquisition days.
result: Problem-informed time choices reveal useful evolution directions missed by ordinary time evolution, though some directions become too similar for reliable estimation; the four-qubit experiment shows a median 54% reduction in projected-energy error relative to uniform sampling under matched hardware conditions.
conclusion: Simulation-basis design is presented as a practical interface between quantum algorithms and noisy hardware, serving as a proof of principle for trial-space co-design rather than a fully general protocol.

title: Decision-aware Validation Of Zero-noise Extrapolation In Qaoa Optimization Landscapes
authors: Vicenzo Scavino Alfaro
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE) is usually validated by the accuracy of mitigated observables, yet variational quantum optimization uses those observables to select parameters. We ask whether, and by how much, an accuracy gain from ZNE coincides with a worse decision. In depth-one simulations of the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) for MaxCut on four to six qubits, each sampled [MATH] landscape yields both its mean-squared error (MSE) and the ideal regret of its selected grid minimum, comparing Richardson orders one to three with unmitigated estimation at the same total shot budget per grid point. In an exploratory screen of 675 conditions, whose per-point random seeds collide, a familywise (Holm) analysis retains only four of 540 replication conditions as showing both directional MSE improvement and regret increase. A frozen confirmation with 100 fresh paired repetitions per condition reproduces all four: median MSE improvements of 7.65-73.09% accompany median normalized regret increases of only 0.0031-0.0073. We distinguish a bias route, in which residual bias reorders the mean landscape, from a variance route, in which Richardson weights amplify finite-shot noise. Exact first and second moments on a bounded control grid find no bias-route reversal: mitigated mean landscapes preserve the ideal minima, and ZNE can more than halve expected MSE, yet finite-shot selections incur higher mean regret. Decision losses that survive strict testing are few and small in this benchmark, but reproducible and not revealed by aggregate MSE. We present a paired benchmark and recommend reporting decision regret alongside estimation error when mitigation is assessed for optimization. Results concern simulated exhaustive grids, not hardware or optimizer loops.
tldr: The paper tests whether zero-noise extrapolation's improved observable accuracy translates into better QAOA parameter decisions, finding small but reproducible decision-regret increases in a narrow simulated benchmark.
motivation: Error mitigation is typically validated by observable accuracy, but variational quantum optimization uses those observables to choose parameters, so accuracy gains may not imply better decisions.
method: Depth-one QAOA MaxCut simulations on four to six qubits compare Richardson ZNE orders one to three against unmitigated estimation at equal shot budgets, using paired MSE and normalized regret over exploratory and frozen confirmation grids.
result: Only four of 540 replication conditions survive strict familywise testing, showing median MSE improvements of 7.65-73.09% alongside small median normalized regret increases of 0.0031-0.0073; no bias-route reversal is found, while finite-shot variance can worsen selections.
conclusion: Decision regret should be reported alongside estimation error when assessing mitigation for optimization, though the results are limited to simulated exhaustive grids rather than hardware or optimizer loops.

title: Designing Quantum Solutions To The Closest String Problem With The Non-Variational Qwoa
authors: Jingbo Wang Benjamin Rossdeutscher
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computing offers promising approaches to combinatorial optimization problems whose search spaces grow exponentially with problem size. The Closest String problem belongs to this category, which seeks a string that minimizes the maximum Hamming distance to any string in a given collection of reference strings. In this work, we present an end-to-end quantum implementation of the Closest String problem using the Non-Variational Quantum Walk Optimization Algorithm (NV-QWOA), evaluating its resource requirements and solution amplification capabilities. Our automated workflow converts arbitrary problem instances into quantum circuits expressed in one- or two-qubit gates that encode candidate solutions, evaluate the objective function, and apply NV-QWOA optimisation to increase the measurement probabilities of high-quality solutions. Analytical resource estimates yield a qubit complexity of [MATH] and a circuit depth of [MATH], where [MATH] is the string length, [MATH] is the number of reference strings, [MATH] is the alphabet size, and [MATH] is the number of NV-QWOA iterations. We introduce a revised prescription for the phase-separation parameter, [MATH], that depends on problem size but requires no instance-specific optimization. This prescription mitigates excessive phase wrapping modulo [MATH], which can weaken the relationship between objective values and the phases guiding the optimization dynamics. Across all simulated problem sizes, the algorithm consistently amplifies optimal and near-optimal candidates. This work provides an explicit gate-level implementation, an improved phase-scaling method, and a foundation for hardware experiments and benchmarking against classical algorithms.
tldr: An end-to-end gate-level implementation of the Closest String combinatorial optimization problem using the Non-Variational Quantum Walk Optimization Algorithm (NV-QWOA), with analytical resource estimates and an improved phase-separation parameter prescription.
motivation: Combinatorial optimization problems like Closest String have exponentially large search spaces, and non-variational quantum walk approaches may avoid the training overhead of variational circuits while amplifying high-quality solutions.
method: The authors build an automated workflow that compiles arbitrary Closest String instances into one- and two-qubit gate circuits encoding candidates, evaluating the Hamming-distance objective, and applying NV-QWOA phase amplification, with a revised problem-size-dependent phase-separation parameter to mitigate phase wrapping mod 2π.
result: Analytical estimates give qubit complexity and circuit depth scaling with string length, number of reference strings, alphabet size, and iteration count; simulations across all tested problem sizes show consistent amplification of optimal and near-optimal candidates.
conclusion: The work provides an explicit circuit construction and improved phase-scaling heuristic, intended as a foundation for hardware experiments and benchmarking against classical algorithms for Closest String.

title: Benchmarking Classical And Quantum Machine Learning For Intrusion Detection Across Multiple Datasets
authors: Naima Kaabouch Taha M. Mahmoud
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intrusion detection is examined through a comparative benchmark of classical and quantum machine learning models on three datasets: NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15, and MQTTEEB-D2025. The analysis focuses on how preprocessing decisions, feature selection strategies, and quantum encoding schemes shape model performance on data with differing levels of noise and complexity. A single unified pipeline is applied, covering normalization, class-imbalance handling, dimensionality reduction, and two feature selection methods: Random Forest importance and a quantum-aware approach that combines Quantum Kernel Alignment with Mutual Information (QKA-MI). Four classifiers are compared: Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, Quantum Support Vector Machine, and Pegasos Quantum SVM. The classical models perform consistently across all three datasets, whereas the quantum models depend more strongly on feature representation and kernel alignment. Quantum-aware feature selection yields marked gains for the quantum models, especially on cleaner datasets, while heterogeneous traffic remains difficult. Pegasos Quantum SVM offers a good trade-off between accuracy and computational cost, underscoring the role of preprocessing alignment in practical quantum intrusion detection.
tldr: This paper benchmarks classical and quantum machine learning models for network intrusion detection across three datasets, emphasizing preprocessing and quantum-aware feature selection.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how preprocessing, feature selection, and quantum encoding choices affect quantum versus classical ML performance on intrusion-detection data with varying noise and complexity.
method: A unified pipeline is applied to NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15, and MQTTEEB-D2025, comparing SVM, Random Forest, Quantum SVM, and Pegasos Quantum SVM with Random Forest importance and QKA-MI feature selection.
result: Classical models perform consistently across datasets, while quantum models are more sensitive to feature representation and kernel alignment; quantum-aware feature selection helps quantum models, especially on cleaner datasets, and Pegasos Quantum SVM offers a favorable accuracy-cost trade-off.
conclusion: Quantum intrusion detection requires careful preprocessing and kernel alignment, and heterogeneous traffic remains challenging; the work is an applied QML benchmark rather than an information-theoretic contribution.

title: An Efficient Quantum Spectral-Galerkin Method For Linear Elliptic Equations
authors: Sheng Chen Dongjie Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents an efficient quantum spectral-Galerkin method for constant-coefficient second-order linear elliptic equations. The method employs a boundary-adapted Jacobi tensor-product basis that incorporates the boundary condition into the approximation space and produces Galerkin systems with polynomially bounded condition numbers and sparsity. For analytic solutions satisfying a suitable uniform regularity condition, spectral convergence allows the normalized Galerkin coefficient state to be prepared with complexity [MATH], where [MATH] is the spatial dimension and [MATH] is the error tolerance, under standard sparse-access and state-preparation assumptions. At the state-preparation level, this improves the precision dependence over fixed-order finite-difference and finite-element discretizations. We further show how to estimate prescribed linear functionals of the solution, with an additional [MATH] factor arising from norm and inner-product estimation.
tldr: A quantum spectral-Galerkin algorithm that prepares the solution of constant-coefficient second-order linear elliptic equations as a quantum state with polylogarithmic error dependence, via a boundary-adapted Jacobi tensor-product basis giving well-conditioned sparse Galerkin systems.
motivation: Classical discretizations such as finite differences and finite elements have fixed-order accuracy, so achieving high precision requires polynomially growing resources; the authors aim to exploit spectral convergence to improve the precision dependence of quantum PDE solvers.
method: The boundary conditions are built directly into a Jacobi tensor-product basis so the resulting Galerkin matrices are sparse and polynomially well-conditioned; assuming sparse-access and state-preparation oracles, the normalized Galerkin coefficient state is prepared and linear functionals of the solution are estimated via norm and inner-product estimation.
result: For analytic solutions obeying a uniform regularity condition, the state-preparation complexity scales polylogarithmically in the error tolerance and polynomially in the spatial dimension, improving on fixed-order finite-difference and finite-element approaches, with an extra polynomial factor for functional estimation.
conclusion: Quantum spectral methods offer a favorable precision scaling for elliptic PDEs, though the gains rest on strong smoothness, sparse-access, and state-preparation assumptions and address numerical analysis rather than quantum-information-theoretic questions.

title: Mds Codes Containing A Fixed Subcode Over Finite Field Extensions
authors: Pingzhi Yuan Yangcheng Li
abstract: ArXiv:2610.34016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] and let [MATH] be a fixed [MATH]-dimensional linear code. We study the [MATH] maximum distance separable (MDS) codes over finite extensions of [MATH] that contain the scalar extension of [MATH]. Our approach constructs an auxiliary linear code from \(U\). Its full-weight words characterize the desired MDS completions. We prove that \(U\) admits an \([n,k]\) MDS completion over some finite extension of \(_q\) if and only if \(d(U)\ge n-k+1\). When this condition holds, the number of these MDS codes over [MATH] is \[\#\left\{W\le_{q^m}^n:U\otimes_{_q}_{q^m}\subseteq W,\ \dim_{_{q^m}} W=k,\ W\right\}=(q^m)}{q^m-1},\] where [MATH] is a generator matrix of [MATH], [MATH] is its represented derived matroid, and [MATH] is its characteristic polynomial. In particular, the formula determines existence over each extension field and the least extension degree for which such an MDS code exists. Examples show that these counts may distinguish different representations of the same column matroid, while monomially inequivalent codes may have identical counts over every finite extension.
tldr: This paper characterizes when a fixed linear code U admits an [n,k] MDS completion over finite extensions of F_q, and counts the number of such MDS codes via a derived matroid and characteristic polynomial.
motivation: MDS codes are optimal in the classical coding-theory sense (maximum distance for given length and dimension), and understanding which subcodes can be embedded into MDS codes over extension fields informs code construction and classification.
method: An auxiliary linear code is constructed from U so that its full-weight codewords characterize valid MDS completions; the count of completions is then expressed through the represented derived matroid of a generator matrix and its characteristic polynomial.
result: U admits an [n,k] MDS completion over some finite extension if and only if d(U) >= n-k+1, and under this condition the number of completions over F_{q^m} is given by a closed formula involving the characteristic polynomial, which also yields the least extension degree required.
conclusion: The counting formula determines existence over each extension field and can distinguish different representations of the same column matroid, while monomially inequivalent codes may share identical counts.

title: The Golomb--Welch Conjecture For Lattice Tilings
authors: Bocong Chen, Jing Huang, Gaojun Luo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Golomb--Welch conjecture for lattice tilings: for every [MATH] and [MATH], the integer lattice [MATH] admits no lattice tiling by Lee balls [MATH] of radius [MATH]. Together with the classical constructions for [MATH] and for [MATH], this determines all parameters for which a lattice Lee tiling exists. Equivalently, we show that every abelian Cayley graph of even degree [MATH] and diameter [MATH] has strictly fewer than [MATH] vertices.
tldr: The authors prove the Golomb–Welch conjecture for lattice tilings, showing no lattice tiling of Z^n by Lee balls of radius R exists for n ≥ 3 and R ≥ 2, thereby settling the exact parameter regime for lattice Lee tilings.
motivation: The Golomb–Welch conjecture, open since 1968, concerns the existence of perfect Lee-metric error-correcting codes, equivalently lattice tilings of the integer lattice by Lee spheres; only the cases n ≤ 2 and R ≤ 1 were previously resolved constructively.
method: The proof is combinatorial/algebraic, translating the tiling question into a statement about the number of vertices in abelian Cayley graphs of even degree and diameter R, and bounding that vertex count strictly below the sphere-packing (Lee ball) volume.
result: For every n ≥ 3 and R ≥ 2, Z^n admits no lattice tiling by Lee balls of radius R; combined with classical constructions for n ≤ 2 and R ≤ 1, this determines all parameters admitting a lattice Lee tiling, and equivalently shows abelian Cayley graphs of even degree 2R and diameter R have fewer than the perfect-code number of vertices.
conclusion: The lattice version of the Golomb–Welch conjecture is fully resolved, completing the classification of lattice Lee tilings, though the general (non-lattice) perfect Lee code problem and any quantum coding analogues remain outside the scope of this work.

title: Securing Edge & Physical Ai: Post-Quantum IoT Blockchain For Mission-Critical Cyber-Physical Agents
authors: Suat \"ozdemir K\"ur\c{s}at \c{c}akal
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) and Edge AI networks increasingly depend on public-key authentication and key-establishment mechanisms that are vulnerable to cryptographically relevant Quantum Computers (QC). Shor's algorithm threatens widely deployed asymmetric primitives, while Grover's algorithm reduces the effective security margins of symmetric and hash-based mechanisms. Although Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) provides a migration path, its larger public keys, ciphertexts, and signatures introduce additional computation, memory, communication, storage, and packet-fragmentation costs that can constrain dynamic multi-agent systems. In this article, we introduce rotational secrecy, an architectural objective that limits temporal key exposure through authenticated transitions between cryptographic epochs. We present Private Authentication for Rotational Secrecy (PARS), a reference mechanism that coordinates policy-triggered key establishment, rotation, and reconciliation among authorized Physical AI agents. For deployments that need distributed agreement on security state, we further develop the PARS-Enabled Edge Security Ledger (PARS-ESL), an optional permissioned architecture maintained by authorized validators or capable edge gateways. PARS-ESL does not store high-volume operational transactions. Instead, it records authenticated state for key epochs, group membership, revocation, algorithm-suite policies, challenge validation, and recovery checkpoints. As a result, resource-constrained agents can take part as lightweight clients, and low-latency operational traffic stays outside the ledger consensus path, protected by the currently active symmetric epoch keys. Our results show that ledger-assisted post-quantum key-epoch management is feasible for selected Edge AI and CPS security-control workloads under the stated trust, compromise, connectivity, and resource assumptions.
tldr: The paper proposes PARS, a policy-driven key-epoch rotation mechanism, plus an optional permissioned ledger (PARS-ESL) for post-quantum-secure authentication among Edge AI and cyber-physical agents.
motivation: Distributed CPS and Edge AI depend on public-key authentication that Shor's and Grover's algorithms undermine, while post-quantum schemes impose heavy key, signature, and bandwidth overheads on resource-constrained multi-agent deployments.
method: The authors define 'rotational secrecy' as limiting temporal key exposure, and design PARS to coordinate policy-triggered key establishment, rotation, and reconciliation among authorized agents; an optional permissioned blockchain ledgers only epoch state, membership, revocation, and suite policies rather than operational traffic.
result: Ledger-assisted post-quantum key-epoch management is shown to be feasible for selected Edge AI and CPS security-control workloads under stated trust, compromise, connectivity, and resource assumptions.
conclusion: Post-quantum key rotation with lightweight ledger-backed state management is a practical migration path for mission-critical cyber-physical agents, though results are workload-specific and assumption-dependent.

title: Quantum Heuristic Separation Of Comb Inequalities For The Travelling Salesman Problem
authors: Victor Drouin-Touchette Yohan Finet
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33188v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Comb inequalities are essential cutting planes for the travelling salesman problem, yet their separation remains computationally challenging. We propose a quantum heuristic separation algorithm for this family of inequalities. The algorithm uses a procedure that prepares a uniform superposition of all combs with a fixed number of teeth using polynomially many gates and qubits. As part of this procedure, we present a circuit that coherently encodes the Hamming weight of a data register in one-hot form in an auxiliary register. The separation algorithm then searches for violated inequalities using the Grover-Mixer Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz. Its running time is polynomial under prescribed polynomial budgets for the number of QAOA rounds, parameter optimization steps and samples gathered, although we provide no evidence that such budgets suffice to find a violated comb with constant probability when one exists. We provide an explicit circuit construction for the mixer unitary, the full problem Hamiltonian and a resource analysis.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum heuristic for separating comb inequalities in the travelling salesman problem using Grover-mixer QAOA and explicit circuit constructions.
motivation: Comb inequalities are important cutting planes for the travelling salesman problem, but their separation is computationally hard, motivating quantum heuristic approaches.
method: The authors construct a uniform superposition over combs with a fixed number of teeth via a polynomial-size circuit, coherently encode Hamming weight in one-hot form, and search for violated inequalities using the Grover-Mixer Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz.
result: They provide explicit circuits for the mixer unitary and problem Hamiltonian, along with a resource analysis and polynomial running time under prescribed budgets for QAOA rounds, parameter optimization, and sampling.
conclusion: The work offers a quantum heuristic algorithm for comb separation but provides no evidence that the prescribed polynomial budgets suffice to find a violated comb with constant probability when one exists.

title: On The Energy Minimizing Problem In Plasma Dynamics
authors: Maurice de Gosson
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33040v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A fundamental question in plasma physics and its applications to fusion theory is to find minimum energy stares of plasma.. Hong Qin has suggested the use of what he calls "Gromov ground states" which take into account the phenomenon of symplectic rigidity, as opposed to Gardner's classical approach which only use volume-preserving diffeomorphisms. Howev4er Qin's approach leads to topological difficulties because his constructions remain in the classical (Hamiltonian) domain. We circumvent these difficulties by introducing a quantum-mechanical formulation of the problem, based on the Wigner transform and the symplectic geometry of Gaussian state.
tldr: The paper reformulates the plasma minimum-energy-state problem in a quantum-mechanical framework using the Wigner transform and the symplectic geometry of Gaussian states to circumvent the topological obstructions of Qin's 'Gromov ground states' approach.
motivation: Finding minimum energy states of plasma is a central problem in fusion theory; Hong Qin's symplectic-rigidity-based 'Gromov ground states' improve on Gardner's volume-preserving approach but lead to topological difficulties because they remain in the classical Hamiltonian domain.
method: The author introduces a quantum-mechanical formulation of the constrained energy-minimization problem, exploiting the Wigner transform and the symplectic geometry of Gaussian states to avoid the classical topological obstructions.
result: A quantum-mechanical reformulation of the plasma energy-minimization problem is obtained that sidesteps the topological difficulties of the purely classical symplectic approach.
conclusion: The Wigner/Gaussian-state formulation offers a viable route to characterizing plasma minimum energy states, though the work lies in plasma physics rather than quantum information science.

title: Semiclassical Dynamics Of Higher-order Squeezing: Self-adjoint Extensions And Coherent Returns
authors: A. E. Teretenkov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Higher-order squeezing Hamiltonians have several self-adjoint realizations, while their classical trajectories reach infinity in finite time. We relate these extension problems through boundary amplitudes and the semiclassical propagation of coherent states. A discrete Fourier transformation gives the sink-to-source ray matrix of each quantum realization. After the first passage through infinity, the full Husimi probability measure converges to point masses on outgoing classical branches, with weights equal to the squared moduli of the matrix entries. The proof combines finite-order approximate tail solutions satisfying the exact extension boundary condition with full-norm Gaussian matching and a square-summable residual estimate. For positive energy, we determine the limit after any fixed number of passages: amplitudes evolve by powers of the unitary ray matrix, not by iterations of its squared-modulus matrix. We also realize these limits by concentrated complex amplitudes for an energy-preserving Liouville extension, distinguishing deterministic classical gluings from coherent boundary mixing.
tldr: The paper analyzes self-adjoint extensions of higher-order squeezing Hamiltonians via semiclassical coherent-state propagation and Husimi-measure limits.
motivation: Higher-order squeezing Hamiltonians admit multiple self-adjoint realizations and have classical trajectories that diverge in finite time, motivating a semiclassical bridge between quantum extensions and classical branches.
method: The author relates extension problems through boundary amplitudes and coherent-state propagation, using discrete Fourier transforms, finite-order tail approximations, Gaussian matching, and residual estimates to characterize the Husimi measure after passages through infinity.
result: After the first passage through infinity, the Husimi probability measure converges to point masses on outgoing classical branches, weighted by squared moduli of ray-matrix entries; for positive energy, amplitudes evolve by powers of the unitary ray matrix.
conclusion: The work distinguishes deterministic classical gluings from coherent boundary mixing and realizes the limits via concentrated complex amplitudes for an energy-preserving Liouville extension.

title: The Coherent State Projection Eigenvalue Theorem
authors: Margaret D. Reid Peter D. Drummond
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent papers have developed a cyclic symmetry projected extension for coherent state representations of bosonic Hilbert space. This extension can greatly reduce sampling errors in phase-space simulations of bosonic quantum systems that have symmetries. Here we prove an eigenvalue theorem for the continuum limit of the projected coherent states. Our intuitively appealing result is that in the continuum limit the projected coherent states are eigenstates of the symmetry generating operator. This result gives a differential identity in phase-space that includes the conserved eigenvalues. Detailed applications of these differential identities to obtaining improved Fokker-Planck and stochastic equations in many-body physics will be given elsewhere.
tldr: The paper proves an eigenvalue theorem for projected coherent states in the continuum limit, showing they are eigenstates of the symmetry-generating operator and yielding phase-space differential identities.
motivation: Projected coherent state representations can reduce sampling errors in phase-space simulations of bosonic quantum systems with symmetries, but their continuum-limit structure needed a rigorous eigenvalue characterization.
method: The authors analyze the continuum limit of cyclic-symmetry-projected coherent states and prove an eigenvalue theorem, deriving a differential identity in phase space that includes conserved eigenvalues.
result: In the continuum limit, projected coherent states are shown to be eigenstates of the symmetry-generating operator, providing phase-space differential identities with conserved eigenvalues.
conclusion: The theorem supplies a mathematical foundation for improved Fokker-Planck and stochastic equations in many-body bosonic simulations, with detailed applications deferred elsewhere.

title: Linear Statistics In The Coulomb Gas: Cumulants Beyond Rotational Invariance
authors: Paul Bourgade, Pierre Le Doussal, Gregory Schehr
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a classical Coulomb gas of [MATH] particles in dimension [MATH], confined by a general external potential [MATH] in the large-[MATH] limit. In that limit the density of particles has a compact support called the droplet. We study smooth linear statistics [MATH] at large [MATH]. While the leading variance of [MATH] is by now well understood in many settings, much less is known about higher cumulants. When [MATH] and the potential is rotationally invariant, these cumulants were computed recently at leading order. We derive explicit formulas for the leading third and fourth cumulants for general smooth droplets, without assuming that either the potential or the test function is radial. The answers are expressed as intrinsic boundary integrals over the equilibrium droplet. The third cumulant depends on the cube of the jump of the normal derivative of the harmonic extension of [MATH], while the fourth cumulant also involves the exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, the mean curvature of the boundary, and normal derivatives of the background density. Our derivation uses the tilted potential [MATH], the associated deformation of the droplet, and shape derivatives of the Dirichlet energy. This deformation has a natural interpretation as the infinitesimal motion of the free boundary in the obstacle-problem formulation of the equilibrium measure. Our formulas extend previous studies by Wiegmann and Zabrodin in two dimensions for [MATH]. In their setting, we provide a rigorous proof of the limiting third and fourth cumulants, supporting the proposed formulas for general Coulomb gases. We specialize the general formulas to the disk, the half-plane and the sphere, and check them against exactly solvable non-radial deformations, including translated elliptic droplets in [MATH] and spheroidal deformations in [MATH].
tldr: The paper derives explicit leading-order formulas for the third and fourth cumulants of smooth linear statistics of a large-N classical Coulomb gas in arbitrary dimension for general (non-radial) droplets, expressed as intrinsic boundary integrals over the equilibrium droplet.
motivation: The variance of linear statistics in Coulomb gases is well understood, but higher cumulants are known only in special cases (2D, rotationally invariant potentials), so a general non-radial theory is needed.
method: The authors use the tilted potential, the associated deformation of the droplet, and shape derivatives of the Dirichlet energy, giving a free-boundary/obstacle-problem interpretation, and check results against exactly solvable non-radial deformations and special geometries (disk, half-plane, sphere).
result: The third cumulant depends on the cube of the jump of the normal derivative of the harmonic extension of the test function, while the fourth additionally involves the exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, boundary mean curvature, and normal derivatives of the background density; these extend Wiegmann–Zabrodin results and are made rigorous.
conclusion: The work provides a general geometric formula for higher cumulants of linear statistics in Coulomb gases, unifying and rigorously extending previous 2D results to arbitrary dimension and non-radial settings.

title: Efficient Block Encodings Of Vibrational Hamiltonians
authors: Shashank G. Mehendale, Ignacio Loaiza, Shreyas Malpathak, Stepan Fomichev, Danial Motlagh, Artur F. Izmaylov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulation of molecular vibrations is emerging as a promising application of quantum computing in quantum chemistry. In this work, we develop new strategies for block-encoding the second-quantized [MATH]-mode representation of the vibrational Hamiltonian, whose algebraic structure closely parallels that of the second-quantized electronic Hamiltonian. We derive linear-combination-of-unitaries (LCU) representations of this Hamiltonian based on Pauli decomposition and tensor hypercontraction (THC) and construct efficient circuits for the corresponding block encodings. We also extend the Block-Invariant Symmetry Shift (BLISS) technique to vibrational Hamiltonians, yielding a lower LCU 1-norm and, consequently, a lower overall circuit cost. For the molecules considered here, BLISS-THC reduces the Toffoli cost of quantum phase estimation by more than two orders of magnitude relative to existing block-encoding approaches. In comparison with recent Trotter-based methods, it shows up to a ninefold reduction in the T-gate count, with the relative savings tending to increase with system size. Asymptotically, and up to polylogarithmic factors, both the Pauli and THC LCUs trade additional ancillas for a quadratic improvement in scaling with the number of modes, while THC provides an additional quadratic improvement in scaling with the number of modals. These results highlight the importance of Hamiltonian factorizations and Toffoli-qubit tradeoffs for reducing the computational cost of quantum simulations of molecular vibrations.
tldr: The paper develops efficient block encodings for second-quantized vibrational Hamiltonians to reduce the cost of quantum simulation of molecular vibrations.
motivation: Quantum simulation of molecular vibrations is a promising quantum-chemistry application, but existing block-encoding and Trotter methods remain costly for realistic vibrational Hamiltonians.
method: The authors derive LCU representations based on Pauli decomposition and tensor hypercontraction (THC), construct block-encoding circuits, and extend the Block-Invariant Symmetry Shift (BLISS) technique to vibrational Hamiltonians.
result: BLISS-THC reduces QPE Toffoli cost by more than two orders of magnitude versus existing block-encoding approaches and shows up to a ninefold T-gate reduction versus recent Trotter methods, with asymptotic quadratic improvements in mode scaling.
conclusion: Hamiltonian factorization and ancilla-Toffoli tradeoffs are important for lowering the computational cost of quantum simulation of molecular vibrations.

title: Quantum Harmonic Analysis And The Differential Operators On Weighted Bergman Spaces Of Bounded Symmetric Domains
authors: Matthew Dawson, Vishwa Dewage, Gestur Olafsson
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop quantum harmonic analysis (QHA) for operators on the parametrized Bergman space [MATH] of a bounded symmetric domain [MATH], extending the theory previously known for the unit ball. Building on this framework, we introduce a class of differential operators acting on operators on [MATH]. Combining these tools, we advance the theory of Toeplitz operators on [MATH]: we establish Toeplitz approximation results via the [MATH]-Berezin transform, construct a differential operator [MATH] that shifts the [MATH]-Berezin transform, and obtain several characterizations of the radial Toeplitz algebra -- including one via the uniformly continuous radial operators, and one via the domain of [MATH].
tldr: The authors develop a quantum harmonic analysis framework for operators on weighted Bergman spaces over bounded symmetric domains and use it to characterize radial Toeplitz algebras.
motivation: Quantum harmonic analysis, previously formulated only for the unit ball setting, is extended to the broader and more symmetric geometry of bounded symmetric domains, where Toeplitz operator theory is less developed.
method: They construct a QHA machinery for operators on the parametrized Bergman space of a bounded symmetric domain, introduce associated differential operators, and analyze the Berezin transform and Toeplitz approximation properties.
result: They obtain Toeplitz approximation results via the Berezin transform, build a differential operator that shifts the Berezin transform, and give several characterizations of the radial Toeplitz algebra, including via uniformly continuous radial operators.
conclusion: The work generalizes quantum harmonic analysis beyond the unit ball and provides new structural results for Toeplitz algebras on bounded symmetric domains.

title: The Ising Lattice Gas And The Surface Diffusion Of Co On Cu(001) At Finite Coverage
authors: S. Miret-Art\'es
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The memory equation of the coherent intermediate scattering function (ISF), derived previously for lattice gases, is applied to the Ising lattice gas under Kawasaki dynamics. The ISF follows the decay of a density wave of adparticles, a superposition of exponential relaxation modes: the decay starts at a rate fixed by a sum rule and is then slowed by a memory. The static structure factor and the effective hop rate are obtained in closed form, exactly along a one-dimensional channel; with the sum rule they give a single exponential, a lower bound on the ISF. Exact relaxation spectra show that this single exponential, built from equilibrium quantities alone, reproduces the correlation time only at weak coupling; only there can a measured dephasing rate be read through the statics. For strong attraction the slow dissolution of clusters lengthens the correlation time up to ninefold, whereas a repulsive layer relaxes nearly as a single mode at its structure peak. The dephasing rate, fitted over a time window where it is nearly constant, approaches the slowest relaxation rate, not the initial one; the sum rule reaches the data only through the area beneath the normalized decay, which defines the correlation time. For CO/Cu(001), the lattice gas reproduces the dephasing rates measured along two crystal directions and requires a nearest-neighbour repulsion of at least [MATH]--[MATH]~meV, whatever the jump rates; the measured rate is then close to the inverse correlation time, and the memory is predicted to grow with coverage.
tldr: The paper applies a memory-equation formalism for the coherent intermediate scattering function to an Ising lattice gas under Kawasaki dynamics in order to model the surface diffusion of CO on Cu(001) at finite coverage.
motivation: Helium-atom/spin-echo measurements of adsorbate dephasing rates on surfaces are hard to interpret because the measured decay mixes intrinsic hopping with cluster formation and memory effects; a tractable lattice-gas theory linking statics to dynamics is needed.
method: The authors solve the memory equation for the intermediate scattering function of an Ising lattice gas with nearest-neighbour interactions, obtaining the static structure factor and effective hop rate in closed form (exactly in 1D), and compare single-exponential approximations and exact relaxation spectra against measured dephasing rates for CO/Cu(001) along two crystal directions.
result: A single exponential built from equilibrium quantities reproduces the correlation time only at weak coupling; strong attraction slows relaxation up to ninefold via cluster dissolution, and the fitted dephasing rate tracks the slowest relaxation rate rather than the initial one. Fitting the CO/Cu(001) data requires a nearest-neighbour repulsion of at least a few meV and predicts memory growth with coverage.
conclusion: Equilibrium statics suffice to extract dephasing rates only in the weak-coupling regime, while strong interactions require the full memory/spectral treatment; the lattice-gas model successfully reproduces the measured anisotropic CO/Cu(001) dephasing rates.

title: Quantum-Relativistic Anomalous Proper Time
authors: Nelson Yokomizo Pablo L. Saldanha
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate surprising consequences of the hypothesis that gravity and proper time obey the quantum superposition principle. We show that, for a massive body prepared in a superposition of two positions and post-selected in a suitable final state, the elapsed proper time in another region of space can assume an anomalous effective value lying outside the range allowed by classical general relativity. Remarkably, the effective elapsed proper time can even become negative, corresponding to an effective evolution backward in time. We also propose an experiment to observe an anomalous effective proper time associated with the internal degrees of freedom of a quantum particle in an interferometer under Earth's gravitational field. The proposed experiment is, in principle, feasible with current technology, and its realization could provide the first experimental evidence of an interplay between quantum mechanics and general relativity beyond the effects of the Newtonian potential in flat spacetime.
tldr: The paper proposes that a massive body in a spatial superposition can induce an anomalous effective proper time, even negative, in another region, and suggests an interferometric experiment to test this in Earth's gravitational field.
motivation: The authors explore consequences of applying the quantum superposition principle to gravity and proper time, aiming to find observable effects beyond the Newtonian potential in flat spacetime.
method: They analyze a massive body prepared in a superposition of two positions and post-selected in a suitable final state, computing the effective elapsed proper time in another region, and propose an interferometer experiment with a quantum particle's internal degrees of freedom.
result: The effective proper time can lie outside the classically allowed range and can even become negative, corresponding to effective backward-in-time evolution; the proposed experiment is argued to be feasible with current technology.
conclusion: The work suggests a possible first experimental signature of quantum-gravity interplay beyond Newtonian effects, but it lies outside the targeted research directions of quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Proof Of The Langberg-M\'edard Conjecture
authors: Sirui Liu, Zongpeng Li, Baochun Li
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In communication networks, network coding allows intermediate nodes to combine messages, achieving transmission rates unattainable by routing alone in many multicast settings. In multiple unicast, where each source sends a message only to its prescribed destination, the precise capability boundary between coding and fractional routing has long remained unresolved. In this context, the Langberg-M\'edard conjecture asserts that if all sources in a directed network transmit independent messages at a common rate and every destination can recover all source messages by network coding, then replacing every arc by an undirected edge of equal capacity yields a network in which fractional routing can simultaneously deliver each source's message to its prescribed destination at the same common rate. We prove the Langberg-M\'edard conjecture for any number of source-destination pairs and arbitrary network topology. More generally, for an undirected network with a given source set and a disjoint set of allowed destinations, we establish a necessary and sufficient cut-capacity condition for simultaneous unit-rate fractional routing under every assignment of an allowed destination to each source. Networks satisfying the hypothesis of the Langberg-M\'edard conjecture necessarily satisfy this cut condition, so the conjecture follows as a direct corollary.
tldr: The paper proves the Langberg-Médard conjecture, showing that for multiple-unicast networks with independent equal-rate sources, network-coding feasibility implies feasibility of fractional routing in the corresponding undirected network.
motivation: The boundary between what network coding can achieve and what fractional routing can achieve in multiple-unicast settings has remained an open problem, with the Langberg-Médard conjecture offering a precise characterization of that boundary.
method: The authors establish a general necessary and sufficient cut-capacity condition for simultaneous unit-rate fractional routing in undirected networks for every assignment of allowed destinations to sources, then show the conjecture's hypothesis implies this condition.
result: The conjecture is proven for any number of source-destination pairs and arbitrary topologies, following as a direct corollary of the general cut-capacity theorem.
conclusion: Fractional routing in the undirected relaxation matches network-coding feasibility for common-rate multiple unicast, resolving a long-standing question in classical network information theory.

title: Bounds On Polynomial Approximations Of The Discrete Logarithm Function
authors: Swastik Kopparty, Rishabh Kothary, Ashutosh Shankar
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33452v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit a classical result of Coppersmith and Shparlinski showing bounds on how well polynomials can approximate the discrete log function. They showed that for any univariate polynomial [MATH] with [MATH], we have: $[MATH][MATH]D[MATH](1+o(1)) \cdot [MATH]D > p/2[MATH]D = 1[MATH]O()[MATH]O(p^{2/5})[MATH](x, dlog(x)) \in _p^2[MATH]Q(X,Y) \in _p[X,Y][MATH]deg(Q) \leq D$ can vanish on, with our new bounds approaching the analogue of the Johnson bound for this problem.
tldr: The paper revisits and sharpens classical Coppersmith–Shparlinski style bounds on how well low-degree polynomials (and bivariate polynomials of bounded degree) over finite fields can approximate or vanish on the discrete logarithm function.
motivation: Approximability of the discrete log by low-degree polynomials underpins lower bounds for pseudorandom generators and hard-core predicates, so improving these bounds tightens our understanding of the computational hardness of discrete log.
method: The authors use techniques from finite-field polynomial method and additive combinatorics, deriving new upper bounds on the number of points (x, dlog(x)) on which a bivariate polynomial of degree at most D can vanish, approaching a Johnson-bound analogue.
result: Improved bounds are obtained for both univariate approximation of the discrete logarithm and for the list of bivariate polynomials of degree ≤ D vanishing on the graph of dlog, improving over the previous O(p^{2/5})-type estimates.
conclusion: The results sharpen the classical picture of polynomial-approximability of discrete log, which has implications for pseudorandomness and hardness results, but they remain in the domain of classical complexity and finite-field combinatorics rather than quantum information theory.

title: Optimal Search Strategies Under Finite Resource Constraints
authors: Hugues Meyer
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Improving target search is a challenge faced by many natural and artificial agents, often requiring the use of energetic or material resources. These inputs may be supplied by an external controller or generated by the searcher itself, for example, through the deposition of cues along its trajectory. Although such resources are commonly modeled as costly but available without an explicit limit, in practice, they can often only be produced in finite amounts. Here, we go beyond the assumption of an unlimited supply of resources by investigating searches in which a finite resource budget must be allocated throughout the search process. To investigate this problem, we equip a one-dimensional diffusive searcher with three types of resources: an external force, a supply of partially reflecting flags, and auto-chemotactic cues. We derive exact optimal resource-allocation protocols for informed search processes in which the agent has continuous access to its past and current positions, which we find to always require resource allocation to be spatially concentrated. We then determine the corresponding protocols for blind searchers and show that resource usage must be more evenly distributed. Non-Markovian cues that generate environmental memory are found to substantially improve search performance when the agent has access to positional information, even under finite-resource constraints. In contrast, their benefits are considerably more limited for blind search, particularly when the cues provide no directional information.
tldr: The paper derives exact optimal resource-allocation protocols for one-dimensional diffusive searchers that must operate under a finite budget of resources such as external forces, partially reflecting flags, and auto-chemotactic cues.
motivation: Existing models of target search treat energetic or material resources as costly but unlimited, whereas in practice agents can only produce or receive finite amounts, so the allocation of a bounded resource budget over the search trajectory needs to be understood.
method: A one-dimensional diffusive searcher is equipped with three resource types (external force, partially reflecting flags, auto-chemotactic cues), and exact optimal allocation protocols are derived separately for informed searchers with continuous positional access and for blind searchers.
result: Informed search always benefits from spatially concentrated resource allocation, whereas blind search requires more evenly distributed usage; non-Markovian cues generating environmental memory substantially improve performance for informed agents but give limited gains for blind searchers lacking directional information.
conclusion: Finite resource budgets qualitatively reshape optimal search strategies, and the value of environmental memory depends strongly on whether the searcher has positional information.

title: Proof Of The Langberg-M\'edard Multiple Unicast Conjecture
authors: Kai Cai, Guangyue Han, Mengxi Yang, Wenan Zang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a directed network, where [MATH] is a digraph, [MATH] is a set of senders, and [MATH] is a set of receivers. We prove that if, for each [MATH], there exist [MATH] pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths in [MATH], one from each [MATH] to [MATH], then the underlying undirected network of [MATH], with unit capacities, admits a feasible [MATH]-[MATH] multiflow of value [MATH] for each pair [MATH], [MATH]. This establishes the multiple unicast conjecture proposed by Langberg and M\'edard in 2009.
tldr: The paper proves the Langberg-Médard multiple unicast conjecture for directed networks under a pairwise arc-disjoint path condition.
motivation: The multiple unicast conjecture in network coding has remained open since 2009; resolving it would clarify the achievable rate region for multiple unicast sessions.
method: The authors use graph-theoretic techniques to show that certain pairwise arc-disjoint directed path conditions imply the existence of feasible multiflows in the underlying undirected unit-capacity network.
result: They prove that if each receiver has pairwise arc-disjoint paths from all senders, then the underlying undirected network admits a feasible multiflow of the required value for every sender-receiver pair.
conclusion: This establishes the Langberg-Médard multiple unicast conjecture, settling a longstanding open problem in classical network coding and multiflow theory.

title: Dynamics Of Two-dimensional Bose Gases In The Focusing Case
authors: Lukas Reichmann
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the propagation of Bose--Einstein condensation and a norm approximation for the dynamics of a Bose gas with localized initial data in two dimensions with singular interactions that may have a small attractive part. We allow the scaling of the interaction to be any polynomial scaling [MATH] for [MATH] and even exponential scaling [MATH] for [MATH]. Our approach covers external potentials that are time-dependent, at most quadratic, and bounded below, including the situation without an external potential.
tldr: This paper proves propagation of Bose-Einstein condensation and norm approximation for two-dimensional Bose gases with singular interactions, including a small attractive part and polynomial or exponential scaling.
motivation: The work addresses the mathematical dynamics of focusing Bose gases in two dimensions with localized initial data and singular interactions, extending rigorous PDE analysis to attractive regimes and general time-dependent external potentials.
method: The author uses rigorous mathematical analysis of nonlinear Schrödinger-type equations to establish BEC propagation and norm approximation under singular interaction scalings.
result: The paper proves BEC propagation and a norm approximation for the dynamics, allowing polynomial and exponential interaction scalings and time-dependent, at most quadratic, bounded-below external potentials.
conclusion: The results provide mathematical justification for the dynamics of two-dimensional focusing Bose gases in a broad scaling regime, but the paper is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Partial Airy Ideals And Coloured Blobbed Topological Recursion
authors: Ga\"etan Borot, Vincent Bouchard, Swagata S. Datta
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define and study the notion of partial Airy ideals, which are certain linear systems of PDEs that may contain less equations than variables. We show that they admit a unique solution of exponential type (the partition function) modulo a choice of initial condition. We construct a large class of examples of partial Airy ideals attached to spectral curves using twisted free-field representations of [MATH]-algebras at self-dual level. This generalizes the results of Bouchard- Borot-Chidambaram-Creutzig-Noshchenko by significantly enlarging the set of admissible spectral curves, provided they come with additional data that we call colour. We show that the differential constraints on the partition function are equivalent to a set of equations on the associated correlators, which we call coloured loop equations. We find a recursive residue formulation for the solutions of those equations, the coloured blobbed topological recursion}, which is a generalization of the currently known forms of topological recursion. It includes the blobbed topological recursion of Borot-Shadrin as a special case, giving it a natural interpretation within the formalism of partial Airy ideals.
tldr: The paper introduces partial Airy ideals — linear systems of PDEs with fewer equations than variables admitting a unique exponential-type partition function — and derives a generalized 'coloured blobbed topological recursion' for their correlators.
motivation: Topological recursion and Airy structures have proven powerful unifying frameworks for generating functions of enumerative geometry and matrix models; the authors aim to enlarge the class of spectral curves for which such PDE-based constructions exist by allowing incomplete systems of equations.
method: They use twisted free-field representations of W-algebras at self-dual level to construct partial Airy ideals attached to spectral curves equipped with extra data called a 'colour', and show the differential constraints translate into coloured loop equations admitting a residue-recursive solution.
result: Existence and uniqueness (modulo initial conditions) of a partition function for partial Airy ideals is established, and the coloured blobbed topological recursion is shown to generalize known forms of topological recursion, with Borot–Shadrin blobbed topological recursion as a special case.
conclusion: Partial Airy ideals provide a natural algebraic home for blobbed topological recursion and substantially widen the admissible set of spectral curves, suggesting further unification of enumerative and integrable structures.

title: Deep-Microscopic Photonic Bandstructure Of A Two-Dimensional Honeycomb Lattice
authors: Pronoy Das, Sathwik Bharadwaj, Wenbo Sun, Zubin Jacob
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional descriptions of light in materials rely on macroscopic models that average the optical response over the microscopic lattice structures. These models are deployed in the semi-classical limit, where the collective local response over many lattice sites is adequate. However, they fail to capture the full spatial dispersion, which requires a lattice-resolved description of light. We address this limitation by formulating a deep-microscopic nonlocal theory of the photon based on the Maxwell Hamiltonian and its characteristic equation. The solution reveals the full spatial dispersion in the form of deep-microscopic photonic bandstructure, and corresponding real-space Bloch field textures. We demonstrate our theory for a two-dimensional (2D) tight-binding model of a gapped honeycomb lattice. Our framework thus extends photons to the same microscopic footing as electrons or phonons, providing a unified route to studying topology, dissipation, and quantum fluctuations of light in dispersive materials.
tldr: The paper develops a deep-microscopic nonlocal photonic bandstructure theory for light in a 2D gapped honeycomb lattice using the Maxwell Hamiltonian.
motivation: Conventional macroscopic optical models average over microscopic lattice structure and cannot capture full spatial dispersion, motivating a lattice-resolved description of photons.
method: The authors formulate a nonlocal photon theory from the Maxwell Hamiltonian and its characteristic equation, solving for deep-microscopic photonic bands and real-space Bloch field textures in a 2D tight-binding honeycomb model.
result: They obtain the full spatial dispersion as a deep-microscopic photonic bandstructure and demonstrate corresponding Bloch field textures for the gapped honeycomb lattice.
conclusion: The framework places photons on a microscopic footing analogous to electrons and phonons, suggesting routes to study topology, dissipation, and quantum fluctuations of light in dispersive materials.

title: Packaging Systems: Intrinsic Structure, Recovery Ranks, And Globalization Theorems
authors: Rongchao Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define packaged structures through carriers, internal units, incidence, candidate spaces, and selected families. A realized packaging system additionally retains a context and formation datum related to its output by a possibly partial, multivalued realization relation. We establish comparison-relative recoverability and non-collapse criteria and an intrinsic refinement-completion theory. For atlas specializations, exact extension becomes a specialization-relative packaging completion problem. Under additional recovery and elimination axioms, we establish general globalization sufficiency criteria and sharp classifications for three classes of compatible finite atlases on a fixed cover [MATH]. A geometric obstruction rank [MATH] yields thresholds [MATH] for empty-preserving closures of local Carath\'eodory number at most [MATH]; [MATH] for complete functional-dependency theories of local minimum Armstrong size at most [MATH]; and [MATH] for transitive relations, including equivalence relations. For nonempty finite label sets and empty-preserving closures, minimum commutant realization dimension equals minimum Armstrong size. We also determine intrinsic recovery ranks and construct canonical clique completions under bounded conformality without chordality. Explicit obstructions establish sharpness; a transport hypothesis is essential for the general recovery--obstruction converse. Complexity bounds apply locally, not necessarily to global extensions.
tldr: The paper introduces 'packaging systems' — a general mathematical framework of carriers, internal units, incidence structures and realization relations — and proves recoverability, refinement-completion and globalization theorems with sharp obstruction-rank thresholds for finite atlases.
motivation: The authors aim to unify and generalize notions of local-to-global extension (in the spirit of sheaf/atlas gluing and database dependency theory) into an abstract 'packaging' formalism, providing intrinsic structure theory and sharp classification results.
method: Abstract structural definitions (carriers, incidence, candidate spaces, selected families, context/formation data, partial multivalued realization relations) combined with axiom-driven theorems: recovery and elimination axioms, refinement-completion theory, geometric obstruction ranks, and complexity bounds for local extensions.
result: Sharp thresholds are derived: obstruction rank bounds for empty-preserving closures of local Carathéodory number, for complete functional-dependency theories via minimum Armstrong size, and for transitive/equivalence relations; moreover, for nonempty label sets minimum commutant realization dimension equals minimum Armstrong size, with canonical clique completions constructed under bounded conformality.
conclusion: The framework yields general globalization sufficiency criteria and sharp classifications for compatible finite atlases on a fixed cover, with explicit obstructions demonstrating sharpness and a transport hypothesis shown to be essential for the recovery–obstruction converse.

title: Classical Cumulants From The Double Tensor Unshuffle Hopf Algebra
authors: Jingtao Li Xing Gao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We realize classical cumulants and their fixed-point equations in the double tensor unshuffle Hopf algebra introduced by Ebrahimi-Fard and Patras, placing classical, free, Boolean, and monotone cumulants in a common algebraic framework. A concatenation perturbation of the functionals yields left and right half-shuffle equations on ordinary words without changing the coproduct or either half-coproduct. Both equations are equivalent to the classical moment--cumulant formula and uniquely determine the classical cumulants. We also obtain a Hopf-algebraic realization of the classical-to-free cumulant transform through convolution exponentiation and the left half-shuffle logarithm. A commutative diagram identifies its partition-level action with summation over non-crossing closure fibers, recovering Lehner's closure-fiber formula within the framework of the double tensor unshuffle Hopf algebra.
tldr: The paper embeds classical cumulants and their fixed-point equations within the double tensor unshuffle Hopf algebra, unifying classical, free, Boolean, and monotone cumulants in one algebraic framework.
motivation: The authors aim to place different notions of cumulants (classical, free, Boolean, monotone) into a common Hopf-algebraic setting and to give a combinatorial realization of the classical-to-free cumulant transform.
method: A concatenation perturbation of the functionals yields left and right half-shuffle equations on ordinary words, without modifying the coproduct or half-coproducts; convolution exponentiation and a left half-shuffle logarithm are used to realize the cumulant transform.
result: Both half-shuffle equations are shown equivalent to the classical moment–cumulant formula and uniquely determine the classical cumulants; a commutative diagram recovers Lehner's closure-fiber formula via summation over non-crossing closure fibers.
conclusion: The work provides a unified Hopf-algebraic treatment of cumulant theories and a partition-level interpretation of the classical-to-free transform, but remains a pure combinatorial-algebraic result.

title: Orthograph Related To Mutual (strong) Numerical Radius Orthogonality On Operator Algebra
authors: Shaoxing Sun, Jinchuan Hou, Xiaofei Qi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] and [MATH] be the algebra of all bounded linear operators on a complex Hilbert space [MATH] and the Jordan algebra of all self-adjoint operators in [MATH], respectively. In this paper, the orthographs by (strong) numerical radius orthogonality relation on [MATH] or [MATH] is introduced, and then the graph-theoretic properties of these orthographs, such as isolated vertices, connected components and the diameters, are discussed.
tldr: The paper introduces orthographs defined by mutual strong numerical radius orthogonality on operator and Jordan algebras and studies their graph-theoretic properties.
motivation: The authors aim to understand structural properties induced by numerical radius orthogonality relations in operator algebras through graph-theoretic invariants.
method: They define orthographs based on mutual strong numerical radius orthogonality for bounded linear operators and self-adjoint operators, then analyze isolated vertices, connected components, and diameters.
result: Graph-theoretic characterizations of these orthographs are obtained, including descriptions of isolated vertices, connected components, and diameter properties.
conclusion: The work contributes to operator theory and numerical radius orthogonality by recasting these relations in graph-theoretic terms, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Noncommutative Algebraic Sets Are Not Generically Nc Manifolds
authors: Jiachen Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A consequence of implicit function theorem is that any algebraic set is a complex manifold except at some singular points which form a strictly lower dimension algebraic subset. Accordingly, an non commutative implicit function theorem of Agler-McCarthy might suggest that a nc algebraic set is generically an nc manifold. However, in this paper, a type of nc polynomials is shown, whose zero locus has larger dimension than the nc manifold given by implicit function theorem.
tldr: The paper shows that noncommutative algebraic sets are not generically noncommutative manifolds, contradicting an intuition suggested by a noncommutative implicit function theorem.
motivation: In commutative algebraic geometry, algebraic sets are manifolds except at lower-dimensional singular loci, so one might expect an analogous generic manifold structure in the noncommutative setting.
method: The author constructs a class of noncommutative polynomials whose zero loci have dimension larger than the noncommutative manifold predicted by the Agler-McCarthy noncommutative implicit function theorem.
result: The constructed examples demonstrate that noncommutative algebraic sets can fail to be generically noncommutative manifolds, with zero loci exhibiting excess dimension.
conclusion: The generic manifold intuition from commutative algebraic geometry does not carry over to noncommutative algebraic sets, revealing a structural distinction in noncommutative geometry.

title: Joint End-to-End Training Of Weighted Bp Decoder Ensembles
authors: Felix Krieg, Paul Bezner, Stephan Ten Brink
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ensemble decoding improves decoding reliability by combining component decoders with complementary failure events. Existing approaches typically obtain this diversity from code-specific structure, such as code automorphisms, multiple parity-check representations, or targeted modifications of the message-passing graph. In this work, we instead learn the diversity of an ensemble of weighted belief propagation decoders by jointly optimizing trainable Tanner-graph edge weights. A central design question is how the training objective should distribute gradient among the ensemble members to promote complementary decoding behavior. To this end, we compare four ensemble objectives under direct gradient-based optimization and identify best-member training as the most effective approach. For a (64,32) progressive edge-growth (PEG) low-density parity-check (LDPC) code, the resulting ensemble outperforms the considered trained and untrained belief-propagation-based ensemble baselines. With 10 members, it provides a gain of approximately 0.66 dB over a single belief propagation decoder at a target frame error rate (FER) of [MATH]. Similar behavior is observed for a (128,64) CCSDS LDPC code, indicating that the learned complementarity is not specific to PEG. Although the ensemble performance improves substantially, all trained members show a higher standalone FER. The gain therefore results from learned specialization and complementary failure events rather than uniformly improved component decoders.
tldr: The paper proposes jointly training ensembles of weighted belief-propagation LDPC decoders to learn complementary failure behavior and improve decoding reliability.
motivation: Ensemble decoding improves reliability by combining decoders with complementary failures, but existing diversity methods rely on code-specific structure rather than learned specialization.
method: The authors optimize trainable Tanner-graph edge weights for an ensemble of weighted BP decoders and compare four ensemble training objectives, identifying best-member training as most effective.
result: For a (64,32) PEG LDPC code, a 10-member trained ensemble achieves about 0.66 dB gain over a single BP decoder at a target FER, with similar behavior on a (128,64) CCSDS LDPC code, though individual members have higher standalone FER.
conclusion: Learned ensemble diversity yields substantial decoding gains through specialization and complementary failure events, even when component decoders are individually weaker.

title: Security Evaluation Of 6G-oriented And O-ran Networks Through Targeted Attacks
authors: Apostolos Valiakos, Dimitrios Psaltis, Alexios Lekidis, Nikolaos Kekatos, Elpiniki Papageorgiou
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The sixth generation (6G) of networks is supported by increased bandwidth, automation through the use of O-RAN technologies. Simultaneously though autonomous operation leads to an extensive threat surface and sophisticated attacks. Understanding the attack impact, the Tactics, Techniques and Procedures that are used by attackers is extremely challenging, but however is crucial for developing defense and mitigation strategies against them. This paper evaluates a targeted attack chain against a virtualized, 6G-oriented O-RAN testbed in which the F1 midhaul interface is accessible to an attacker and transport-layer protection is not enabled. The attack disrupts the legitimate O-DU association, introduces a rogue O-DU using observed configuration parameters, and intercepts user-plane traffic. The attack was evaluated in a fully virtualized testbed based on Open5GS, the srsRAN Project, FlexRIC, and an Electric Vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure based on OCPP 1.6.
tldr: The paper evaluates a targeted attack chain against a virtualized 6G-oriented O-RAN testbed with an exposed F1 midhaul interface, showing how an adversary can hijack O-DU association and intercept user-plane traffic.
motivation: 6G networks rely on O-RAN automation, which expands the attack surface; understanding attacker tactics and their impact is needed to design defenses.
method: A fully virtualized testbed built from Open5GS, srsRAN, FlexRIC, and an OCPP 1.6 EV-charging infrastructure was used to execute a multi-stage attack: disrupting legitimate O-DU association, deploying a rogue O-DU with observed configuration parameters, and intercepting user-plane traffic.
result: The attack chain succeeded against the unprotected transport layer, demonstrating practical compromise of O-RAN midhaul connectivity and user-data confidentiality.
conclusion: Transport-layer protection and midhaul hardening are essential for 6G/O-RAN deployments; the testbed provides a reusable platform for evaluating such threats.

title: Optical Imaging With Only The Evanescent Fields And Without Diffraction
authors: Mufei Xiao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report on a conceptual framework for optical imaging utilizing exclusively evanescent fields, effectively eliminating or attenuating standard optical diffraction. We present the theoretical foundation of this concept based on the decomposition of dipole radiation into evanescent fields and homogeneous propagating waves, exploring the explicit conditions required to suppress the latter. By successfully decoupling and removing the homogeneous component, optical tasks, such as sub-diffraction imaging, can be executed solely via evanescent channels, bypassing traditional diffractive limits. We discuss the physical feasibility of this approach and provide concrete examples of how this conjecture can be realized using currently available laboratory and industrial techniques. The realization of this concept promises to redefine core paradigms in optics and fundamental physics. Because the minimum achievable feature size is no longer governed by the operating wavelength, this approach enables an unprecedented increase in spatial resolution, offering a direct pathway to advance state-of-the-art semiconductor lithography and chip manufacturing.
tldr: The paper proposes a conceptual framework for optical imaging that relies exclusively on evanescent fields by decomposing dipole radiation and suppressing the homogeneous propagating component, thereby circumventing the diffraction limit.
motivation: Conventional far-field imaging is restricted by the diffraction limit, which ties the resolvable feature size to the operating wavelength; the author aims to remove or attenuate the propagating (diffractive) part of the field to achieve sub-diffraction resolution.
method: The approach is a theoretical decomposition of dipole radiation into evanescent and homogeneous propagating waves, with an analysis of the conditions under which the homogeneous component can be decoupled and suppressed, plus discussion of laboratory/industrial implementations.
result: The author argues that imaging tasks such as sub-diffraction imaging can be carried out solely through evanescent channels, and sketches concrete schemes feasible with current technology; no quantitative demonstration or experimental data are provided.
conclusion: The work claims a pathway to wavelength-independent spatial resolution with potential impact on semiconductor lithography and chip manufacturing, framed as a conceptual conjecture rather than a validated result.

title: Weak Type $(1,1)$ Estimates For Noncommutative Maximal Truncated Rough Singular Integrals
authors: Wei Li Junming Cao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33284v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a weak type [MATH] estimate for maximal truncations of noncommutative rough singular integrals whose angular kernels satisfy the classical [MATH] integrability and cancellation conditions. The main ingredient of the proof is a new linearization method for handling the maximal truncations acting on the bad functions arising from the noncommutative Calder\'on--Zygmund decomposition.
tldr: The paper proves weak type (1,1) bounds for maximal truncations of noncommutative rough singular integrals with L log L angular kernels.
motivation: Noncommutative Calderón–Zygmund theory lacks weak-type endpoint estimates for maximal truncated rough singular integrals, which are needed to complete the classical picture in the operator-algebraic setting.
method: The authors introduce a new linearization technique to control maximal truncations acting on 'bad' functions produced by the noncommutative Calderón–Zygmund decomposition, combined with the standard L log L integrability and cancellation conditions on the angular kernel.
result: A weak type (1,1) estimate is established for these maximal truncated noncommutative rough singular integral operators.
conclusion: The work extends classical rough singular integral theory to the noncommutative maximal setting, providing a framework likely applicable to further endpoint estimates in operator-valued harmonic analysis.

title: Holo-NN: Holographic Nearest Neighbor Search Via Compressive Sensing
authors: Bryant Gipson
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the age of AI, privacy-preserving approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search over high-dimensional embeddings has emerged as a critical yet frustratingly challenging domain, dominated by tradeoffs between speed, privacy, and accuracy. Traditional tree and graph-based indexing structures (e.g., HNSW, ScaNN) rely fundamentally on non-linear operations that are computationally intractable under Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) or blind server-side constraints. In this paper, we introduce Holo-NN (Holographic Nearest Neighbor Search), an algebraic framework that replaces data-dependent branching with a single linear projection. Our key observation is that while distances across a database are dense, neighborhood membership is inherently sparse: only a handful of points ever lie close to a query. By pairing locality-preserving feature transforms with Compressive Sensing, Holo-NN folds the entire database offline into a compact holographic sensing matrix.
