At query time, encrypted search reduces to a single, non-interactive matrix-vector multiplication---requiring no FHE bootstrapping, no multi-round interaction, and no client-side index state. This turns private retrieval into an embarrassingly parallel, accuracy-tunable computation that runs out of the box on both CPUs and GPUs, scaling efficiently to production databases. We offer a comparison against other state-of-the-art Private ANN algorithms to help situate the method in the broader context of production-grade private retrieval.
tldr: Holo-NN is a classical algebraic framework that replaces tree/graph-based approximate nearest neighbor indexing with a single linear projection built from locality-preserving transforms and compressive sensing, so that encrypted retrieval reduces to one matrix-vector multiplication compatible with fully homomorphic encryption.
motivation: Privacy-preserving approximate nearest neighbor search over high-dimensional embeddings is bottlenecked by non-linear, data-dependent branching in indexes like HNSW and ScaNN, which is intractable under FHE or blind server-side constraints.
method: The authors exploit the sparsity of neighborhood membership relative to dense pairwise distances, folding the database offline into a compact 'holographic' sensing matrix by combining locality-preserving feature transforms with compressive sensing, so that queries become a single non-interactive matrix-vector product requiring no bootstrapping or client-side index state.
result: The approach yields an embarrassingly parallel, accuracy-tunable private retrieval scheme that runs on CPUs and GPUs and is benchmarked against state-of-the-art private ANN algorithms to situate it among production-grade private retrieval methods.
conclusion: Linear algebraic sketching offers a practical alternative to branching-based indexes for encrypted search, trading some accuracy for large gains in computational simplicity and scalability.

title: A New Analytical Finding For The Born-Infeld Integral Potential
authors: Leonardo Paulo Guimar\~aes de Assis, Priscila Vald\^enia Dos Santos, Sergio de Oliveira Vellozo, Jos\'e Abdala Helay\"el Neto
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A new finding regarding the Born-Infeld potential for short range distances from the charge revealed that its integral form can be almost exact written as the difference between a Coulomb-type potential and a Yukawa-type potential. This allowed for an immediate physical interpretation in terms of classical vacuum polarization and an effective mass. Subsequently, a new U(r) is proposed to cover the entire space. This formulation is then applied to calculate, in a closed manner, the first-order energy shifts in hydrogen-like atoms; a comparison of these shifts with high-precision spectroscopic data provides a model-dependent lower bound for the maximum field intensity parameter b.
tldr: The paper derives an analytical approximation of the Born-Infeld electrostatic potential as a Coulomb-minus-Yukawa form and uses it to compute first-order energy shifts in hydrogen-like atoms, yielding a spectroscopic bound on the Born-Infeld field-strength parameter b.
motivation: The Born-Infeld integral potential for short distances lacks a transparent analytic form, hindering physical interpretation and precision tests of nonlinear electrodynamics.
method: The integral potential is rewritten approximately as the difference of a Coulomb and a Yukawa potential, reinterpreted as classical vacuum polarization with an effective mass, then a global U(r) is proposed and used in first-order perturbation theory for hydrogenic energy levels, compared against high-precision spectroscopic data.
result: Closed-form first-order energy shifts are obtained and comparison with precision spectroscopy gives a model-dependent lower bound on the maximum field intensity parameter b.
conclusion: The Coulomb-minus-Yukawa decomposition offers an intuitive reading of Born-Infeld nonlinearities and enables atomic-spectroscopy constraints, though the bounds remain model-dependent.

title: Fractional Reversible Chemical Kinetics: Time-Driven Monte Carlo Method And Application To Enzyme Conformational Dynamics
authors: Higor V. M. Ferreira Nelson H. T. Lemes
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we present a fractional framework for reversible two-state chemical kinetics derived from the Continuous-Time Random Walk (CTRW) formalism with Mittag-Leffler waiting-time distributions. This derivation provides a microscopic basis for the fractional kinetic equations governed by the Caputo derivative. An exact analytical solution is obtained, yielding closed-form expressions for the time evolution of the state populations. To the best of our knowledge, a time-driven Monte Carlo algorithm is developed for the first time to simulate the irreversible underlying non-Markovian stochastic dynamics governed by a system of Caputo fractional differential equations. The proposed framework is applied to the conformational dynamics of the TbQSOX enzyme, whose relaxation exhibits power-law behavior. The fractional model accurately reproduces the experimental kinetics, providing an estimate of the fractional order [MATH], which is consistent with the observed anomalous dynamics.
tldr: The paper develops a fractional Continuous-Time Random Walk framework for reversible two-state chemical kinetics and applies it to enzyme conformational dynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a microscopic stochastic basis for fractional kinetic equations governed by Caputo derivatives and to simulate non-Markovian dynamics.
method: They derive an exact analytical solution for two-state fractional kinetics and introduce a time-driven Monte Carlo algorithm for the underlying non-Markovian stochastic process.
result: The model reproduces experimental relaxation kinetics of the TbQSOX enzyme and yields an estimate of the fractional order consistent with anomalous dynamics.
conclusion: The fractional CTRW framework offers a useful modeling and simulation tool for anomalous chemical and biochemical kinetics, but it is outside quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Isomorphisms Of $\ell^1$-crossed Products Of Topological Systems
authors: Tabar\'e Roland Eusebio Gardella
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a complete description of the isometric isomorphisms between the [MATH]-crossed products of actions of discrete groups on nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces. In particular, two such crossed products are isometrically isomorphic as Banach algebras if and only if the actions are topologically isomorphic. It follows that [MATH] remembers not just [MATH] but even the acting group and the action, and is not determined by the transformation groupoid [MATH] alone. The proof recovers [MATH] from the hermitian elements and uses the geometry of [MATH]-spaces to identify the invertible isometries. We also obtain analogous results for measurable actions.
tldr: The paper classifies isometric isomorphisms of ℓ¹-crossed products of discrete group actions on compact Hausdorff spaces, showing they encode the acting group and action.
motivation: The work aims to determine how much information about a topological dynamical system is retained by its ℓ¹-crossed product as a Banach algebra.
method: The author recovers the underlying space from hermitian elements and uses the geometry of ℓ¹-spaces to identify invertible isometries between crossed products.
result: Two such crossed products are isometrically isomorphic iff the corresponding actions are topologically isomorphic; analogous results are obtained for measurable actions.
conclusion: The ℓ¹-crossed product remembers not only the space but also the acting group and action, and is not determined solely by the transformation groupoid.

title: Gibbs Measures On Cayley Trees And Homoclinic Orbits
authors: Pietro Majer Alberto Abbondandolo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33287v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the question of existence and multiplicity of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures on Cayley trees with spin space [MATH]. We prove that, under a natural summability assumption on the interaction function, there are always at least two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying two natural symmetry conditions. Moreover, any two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying a suitable non-degeneracy assumption can be superimposed and produce infinitely many other homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures. When the interaction function [MATH] has bounded support in [MATH], there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a symplectomorphism of [MATH], where [MATH] is the smallest natural number such that [MATH] for every [MATH]. For [MATH], results from symbolic dynamics and horseshoes imply the existence of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures whose single-site marginal is concentrated near an arbitrary finite subset of [MATH], where [MATH] is a sufficiently large integer. In the case of interaction functions with infinite support, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a Lagrangian correspondence on the cotangent bundle of a Banach space.
tldr: The paper studies existence and multiplicity of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures on Cayley trees and relates them to homoclinic orbits of symplectic/Lagrangian dynamical systems.
motivation: The work addresses a mathematical statistical-mechanics question about Gibbs measures on tree graphs, with connections to symbolic dynamics and symplectic geometry.
method: It uses summability and non-degeneracy assumptions on interaction functions, symplectomorphisms and Lagrangian correspondences, and symbolic-dynamical arguments such as horseshoes.
result: Under natural assumptions, at least two symmetric homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures exist; bounded-support interactions yield a correspondence with homoclinic orbits, and infinite-support interactions with orbits of a Lagrangian correspondence on a Banach cotangent bundle.
conclusion: The paper provides structural results on Gibbs measures on Cayley trees via dynamical-systems techniques, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Remarks On Covariant Differential Calculus On The Non-standard Quantum Podle\'s Sphere
authors: R\'eamonn \'O Buachalla Tomasz Brzezinski
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An [MATH]-covariant first-order differential calculus on the non-standard quantum Podle\'s two-sphere is constructed. The module of one-forms is explicitly given in terms of modules of sections of charge [MATH] line bundles associated to the quantum Hopf fibration.
tldr: The paper constructs an SU(2)-covariant first-order differential calculus on the non-standard (Podleś) quantum two-sphere, expressing the bimodule of one-forms via sections of charge line bundles over the quantum Hopf fibration.
motivation: Noncommutative differential calculi are needed to define geometry, gauge theory and field theories on quantum spaces, and the non-standard Podleś sphere lacked an explicitly covariant first-order calculus of this type.
method: The authors build the calculus algebraically using the quantum Hopf fibration, identifying the bimodule of one-forms with modules of sections of associated charge line bundles, and verify covariance under the Hopf algebra action.
result: An explicit description of the one-form bimodule and the covariant derivative structure is obtained for the non-standard quantum Podleś sphere, in direct analogy with the standard Podleś case.
conclusion: The construction provides a concrete geometric tool for noncommutative geometry on quantum spheres, but stays within pure quantum-group algebra with no bearing on quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Zeros Of Melnikov Functions For Periodically Perturbed Hamiltonian Systems With Random Coefficients
authors: Erik Lundberg Ali Ittayem
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Introducing a probabilistic perspective on a classical theme within the study of chaotic dynamics, we investigate the zeros of the Melnikov distance function associated to a periodically perturbed Hamiltonian system when the perturbation has random coefficients. We provide asymptotic estimates (as the period of the perturbation becomes large or small) for the average number of zeros and for the probability of no zeros.
tldr: The paper studies zeros of Melnikov functions for periodically perturbed Hamiltonian systems with random coefficients.
motivation: It introduces a probabilistic perspective on a classical topic in chaotic dynamics by analyzing Melnikov distance functions under random perturbations.
method: The authors derive asymptotic estimates for the average number of zeros and the probability of no zeros as the perturbation period becomes large or small.
result: They provide asymptotic formulas characterizing how random coefficients affect the expected zero count and zero-free probability of the Melnikov function.
conclusion: The work contributes probabilistic methods to classical chaotic dynamics but has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Ring-0 By Default: Agents As Operating Systems (AaOS)
authors: Xiang Li, Aichun Huang, Zuyao Xu, Fasheng Miao, Zheli Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents now read and write files, start processes and subagents, fetch network content, load third-party extensions, and save and resume state, which are the responsibilities of an operating system. They gained these functions within about three years, but not the protections that operating systems built over five decades: whatever the model outputs, whether it follows the user, a tool result, or a downloaded skill, runs with the full authority of the host user, in effect at ring 0. Prior work builds an operating system for agents (OS4A); we argue that a deployed agent already is like an operating system (AaOS) and analyze it as one. Taking the mechanisms of standard OS textbooks as a checklist, we map 116 mechanisms in 19 subsystems to their agent counterparts, from product documentation, source code, and the literature, and label each as isomorphic, degraded (function present, protection dependent on the model), missing, mutated, or novel. Only 11 are isomorphic and 65 are missing, most of them protections: privilege separation, resource quotas, transactions, and tamper-proof audit. Existing defenses confine the whole agent or review its extensions and leave this interior unprotected, and by Anderson's reference-monitor criteria (non-bypassable, tamper-proof, verifiable), rules written in the prompt satisfy none. We test the map with thirteen experiments on Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI, covering 25 mechanisms whose enforcement documentation cannot settle: 16 match the analysis, 7 gain a more precise description, and 2 change verdict. Checks sit in single tools, so the shell bypasses them; all three CLIs load forged transcript records on resume; and task control, sub-agent permissions, and model-based monitors are weak. We identify five problems for which no OS defense transfers and derive a prioritized list of open problems from the gaps of the map.
tldr: The paper argues that deployed LLM agents already function as operating systems (AaOS) and shows, by mapping 116 OS mechanisms onto agent counterparts and running 13 experiments on Claude Code, Codex CLI and Gemini CLI, that most OS-style protections are simply missing.
motivation: Agents now read/write files, spawn subprocesses, fetch network content and load third-party extensions, yet everything the model emits executes with full host-user authority — effectively at ring 0 — without the privilege separation, quotas, transactions or tamper-proof audit that five decades of OS design produced.
method: A systematic mapping of OS textbook mechanisms (116 mechanisms across 19 subsystems) to agent implementations, drawn from product documentation, source code and literature, each labelled isomorphic/degraded/missing/mutated/novel, followed by thirteen targeted experiments probing 25 mechanisms whose enforcement the documentation cannot settle.
result: Only 11 mechanisms are isomorphic while 65 are missing, most of them protections; tool-level checks are bypassed by the shell, all three CLIs load forged transcript records on resume, and sub-agent permissions and model-based monitors are found weak.
conclusion: Because prompt-level rules fail Anderson's reference-monitor criteria, agent systems need a genuine interior reference monitor; the authors identify five problems for which no OS defense transfers and derive a prioritized open-problem list.

title: A Twisted Affine Interpolation Of The $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded Integrable Super-Liouville And super-Sinh-Gordon Equations
authors: Naruhiko Aizawa, Ren Ito, Luiza Miranda, Francesco Toppan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is a third one in a series devoted to the construction of [MATH], [MATH]-graded, integrable Toda field theories. The first paper introduced parabosonic models obtained from Rittenberg-Wyler color Lie algebras; the second paper explained how to deal with parafermions (the [MATH]-graded super-Liouville theory) from finite Rittenberg-Wyler color Lie superalgebras. This new paper extends the construction to the infinite case of (twisted) affine color Lie superalgebras. A [MATH]-graded extension of [MATH] allows to interpolate the super-Liouville and the super-Sinh-Gordon models, recovered as special limits. The [MATH]-graded extensions of three frameworks are here discussed: the Polyakov's soldering, the Leznov-Savel'ev Lax pair (zero-curvature) formulation and the B\"acklund transformations. As a byproduct of the construction, the Hamiltonian reduction from the [MATH]-graded [MATH] WZNW models induces a [MATH]-graded color Lie superalgebra which admits three inequivalent superVirasoro subalgebras; they are the [MATH] superVirasoro, the [MATH] [MATH]-graded superVirasoro and the [MATH] [MATH]-graded superVirasoro.
tldr: This paper constructs twisted affine Z_2^2-graded integrable Toda field theories that interpolate between super-Liouville and super-Sinh-Gordon models.
motivation: The work extends a series on graded integrable Toda field theories from finite color Lie algebras and superalgebras to infinite twisted affine color Lie superalgebras.
method: The authors develop Z_2^2-graded extensions of Polyakov soldering, the Leznov-Savel'ev zero-curvature/Lax pair formulation, and Bäcklund transformations.
result: The construction yields a Z_2^2-graded color Lie superalgebra with three inequivalent superVirasoro subalgebras via Hamiltonian reduction from graded WZNW models.
conclusion: The paper provides a mathematical framework for interpolating super-Liouville and super-Sinh-Gordon models within a graded affine integrable field theory setting.

title: Quantitative Resolvent Calculus For Sample Covariance Matrices
authors: Nina D\"ornemann Thomas Stark
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we develop a quantitative resolvent calculus for sample covariance matrices tailored to applications in high-dimensional statistics. We treat single resolvents, their derivatives, and products of two resolvents with different spectral parameters in the proportional-dimensional regime. Our bounds hold uniformly over compact subsets of [MATH] with approximation errors of order [MATH] for deterministic test matrices [MATH]. These bounds require only uniformly bounded fourth moments and a uniformly bounded population covariance operator norm. Neither regular spectral edges nor convergence of the population spectral distribution is required. As a key technical ingredient, we develop an averaging argument for centered quadratic forms involving one or two leave-one-out resolvents. Applications of our results include precision-matrix shrinkage, prediction risk in ridge regression, and generalized cross-validation. For these problems, we obtain quantitative guarantees for estimation and data-driven parameter selection.
tldr: The paper develops a quantitative resolvent calculus for sample covariance matrices in the proportional-dimensional regime, with applications to high-dimensional statistics such as precision-matrix shrinkage and ridge regression.
motivation: High-dimensional statistics requires sharp, uniform control of resolvents of sample covariance matrices under weak moment assumptions, without relying on regular spectral edges or convergence of the population spectral distribution.
method: The authors prove bounds for single resolvents, their derivatives, and products of two resolvents with distinct spectral parameters, using an averaging argument for centered quadratic forms involving one or two leave-one-out resolvents, requiring only bounded fourth moments and bounded population covariance norm.
result: They obtain uniform approximation errors of order 1/sqrt(n) over compact spectral subsets for deterministic test matrices, and derive quantitative guarantees for precision-matrix shrinkage, ridge-regression prediction risk, and generalized cross-validation.
conclusion: The resolvent calculus provides a flexible, assumption-light toolkit for high-dimensional statistical estimation and data-driven parameter selection, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum hardware.

title: A New Family Of Deformed Trigonometric Functions And Their Corresponding Pythagorean-like Relations: Application To The Nonlinear Harmonic Oscillator
authors: P. R. Gordoa, A. Pickering, D. Puertas-Centeno, E. V. Toranzo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we present an extension of the classical trigonometric functions which include, amongst others, the Lindqvist p-trigonometric functions. Additionally, we show their relevance in the study of certain versions of the nonlinear harmonic oscillator equation. Furthermore, we study their more important mathematical properties and obtain their corresponding Pythagorean-like relations. We also define a new extension of the Beta and Ateb sine functions using these new [MATH]-trigonometric functions. Indeed, these new Beta and Ateb functions are involved in the closed form expressions obtained for the solutions of the nonlinear oscillator under certain constraints.
tldr: The paper introduces a new family of deformed trigonometric functions and derives Pythagorean-like identities, applying them to nonlinear harmonic oscillator equations.
motivation: The authors aim to extend classical trigonometric functions, including Lindqvist p-trigonometric functions, and to provide closed-form solutions for certain nonlinear harmonic oscillator models.
method: They define new deformed trigonometric functions, study their mathematical properties, derive Pythagorean-like relations, and use them to extend Beta and Ateb sine functions.
result: The new functions yield closed-form expressions for solutions of the nonlinear harmonic oscillator under specific constraints, along with generalized Beta and Ateb functions.
conclusion: The work is a mathematical contribution to special functions and nonlinear oscillator theory, with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Derivative-Informed Dimension Reduction Of Stochastic Differential Equations: A Path-Space Sensitivity Approach
authors: Joanna Zou, Han Cheng Lie, Youssef Marzouk
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncertainty in the drift of a stochastic differential equation (SDE) induces uncertainty in statistical observables defined as expected functionals on path space. We propose a derivative-informed method for identifying low-dimensional structure in the drift-to-observable map, with the aim of improving the tractability of uncertainty quantification. This approach can be viewed as a generalization of the active subspace method to infinite-dimensional input spaces and to path-space observables of SDEs. Representing uncertainty in the drift by random perturbations in a Hilbert space, we construct a path-space sensitivity operator using first-order Fr\'echet derivatives of the observable with respect to the perturbation. We establish conditions under which the leading eigenfunctions of this operator correspond to directions of maximum mean squared sensitivity of the observable, thus enabling low-dimensional approximation with certified error bounds. We further introduce a martingale control variate of the Fr\'echet derivative that reduces error in sample-based estimators of the operator. Using a Galerkin scheme for numerical discretization, we show that reduced representations of the drift from the derivative-informed basis yield more accurate approximations of mean first hitting times of SDEs than the Karhunen-Lo\`eve expansion of the same truncation order.
tldr: The paper develops a derivative-informed dimension-reduction method for stochastic differential equations by constructing a path-space sensitivity operator for drift uncertainty.
motivation: Uncertainty in SDE drift induces uncertainty in path-space observables, and quantifying this is computationally challenging due to infinite-dimensional input spaces.
method: The authors generalize active subspaces using first-order Fréchet derivatives to define a path-space sensitivity operator, establish conditions for low-dimensional approximation with error bounds, and introduce a martingale control variate plus Galerkin discretization.
result: Derivative-informed reduced drift representations outperform Karhunen-Loève truncation of the same order for approximating mean first hitting times in numerical examples.
conclusion: The approach provides certified low-dimensional approximations for SDE observables and improves sample-based estimator accuracy via control variates.

title: Maximizing Measures For Subadditive And Almost-Additive Potentials On Countable-Alphabet Subshifts
authors: Juliano S. Gonschorowski Ricardo Freire
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the existence of maximizing measures for subadditive and almost-additive families of upper semicontinuous, bounded-above potentials [MATH] on closed subshifts over countable alphabets. Under a coercivity condition on [MATH], we prove that every maximizing sequence, that is, [MATH] satisfying [MATH], is uniformly tight, preventing mass from escaping to arbitrarily large symbols. As a consequence, a maximizing measure exists.
tldr: The paper proves existence of maximizing measures for subadditive and almost-additive families of upper semicontinuous potentials on closed subshifts over countable alphabets, using a coercivity condition to ensure uniform tightness.
motivation: Maximization of ergodic averages of (sub)additive potentials is a central problem in thermodynamic formalism and ergodic optimization, but existing existence results largely assume finite or compact alphabets, leaving countable-alphabet subshifts open.
method: The authors work in the setting of closed subshifts over countable alphabets with bounded-above upper semicontinuous potentials, impose a coercivity condition, and show every maximizing sequence is uniformly tight so that mass cannot escape to arbitrarily large symbols.
result: Under coercivity, uniform tightness of all maximizing sequences is established, which yields the existence of a maximizing measure for both subadditive and almost-additive potential families.
conclusion: The results extend ergodic-optimization existence theorems to countable-alphabet symbolic dynamics, providing a compactness argument based on tightness rather than compactness of the alphabet.

title: On The Stability Of Rank-one Factors For Anosov $\mathbb Z^k$-actions
authors: Jiesong Zhang Danijela Damjanovic
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove [MATH]-stability of [MATH] rank-one factors for a large class of higher rank Anosov [MATH]-actions. If the factor is a projection of a smooth fiber bundle and the action contains an element which acts as the identity on the rank-one factor and is Anosov on every fiber, then any sufficiently [MATH]-small [MATH] perturbation of the action will also have a [MATH] rank-one factor. In particular, we prove the [MATH]-stability of the product structure for Anosov [MATH]-actions which are obtained as a (diagonal) product of two [MATH]-Anosov actions.
tldr: The paper proves stability of rank-one factors for higher-rank Anosov Z^k-actions under small perturbations.
motivation: The work addresses rigidity and structural stability questions for higher-rank Anosov actions and their invariant factor structures.
method: It uses smooth fiber-bundle projections and perturbations, assuming an action element that is identity on the rank-one factor and Anosov on every fiber.
result: Sufficiently small perturbations of the action retain a corresponding rank-one factor, implying stability of product structures for diagonal products of two Anosov actions.
conclusion: The results establish stability of rank-one factors and product structures for a broad class of higher-rank Anosov Z^k-actions.

title: On The Transformation Of Unbounded Convergent Sequences By Linear Operators On Banach Lattices
authors: Ewerton Torres Fabr\'icio Santos
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a weak variant of the concept of unbounded Dunford-Pettis linear operators, which we call unbounded weak Dunford-Pettis operators. We investigate the properties of this new class, establish inclusion and coincidence results involving unbounded Dunford-Pettis operators, and examine its relationship with the class of unbounded absolutely weakly continuous operators.
tldr: The paper introduces a weak variant of unbounded Dunford-Pettis operators on Banach lattices and studies its structural properties.
motivation: The authors aim to extend the theory of unbounded Dunford-Pettis operators by defining an unbounded weak Dunford-Pettis class, motivated by the broader program of 'unbounded' convergence in Banach lattice operator theory.
method: Purely functional-analytic techniques: definition of the new operator class, derivation of inclusion and coincidence theorems, and comparison with unbounded absolutely weakly continuous operators.
result: New inclusion and coincidence relations between unbounded weak Dunford-Pettis operators, unbounded Dunford-Pettis operators, and unbounded absolutely weakly continuous operators are established.
conclusion: The new class fits coherently into the existing hierarchy of unbounded operator classes on Banach lattices, though no physical or information-theoretic application is discussed.

title: First-order Methods For Variational Inequality Problems With Semi-Infinite Constraints
authors: Digvijay Boob Dureksha Thilakasiri
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies first-order methods for monotone variational inequalities with semi-infinite constraints and presents this model as a framework covering constrained saddle-point problems, robust optimization, distributionally robust function-constrained optimization, and generalized Nash equilibrium formulations. Since feasibility must hold over infinitely many indexed constraints, direct projection onto the full feasible region is generally difficult. Therefore, we propose a single-loop primal-dual constraint extrapolation method (PD-ConEx) that updates primal variables, Lagrange multipliers, and worst-case constraint indices using first-order information, linearization, extrapolation, and projections only onto simple sets. We establish convergence guarantees for smooth and nonsmooth regimes, showing how the achievable rates depend on strong monotonicity and strong concavity of the index block. For coupled convex-concave saddle-point problems, strong convexity in the minimization block can accelerate its smooth terms even without strong concavity in the maximization block. We also develop an adaptive smooth variant with [MATH] VI-gap and feasibility guarantees without an a priori bound on generated multipliers. Moment-based and Wasserstein distributionally robust models fit within the framework, and numerical experiments on robust quadratic instances and distributionally robust learning illustrate the method's optimality and feasibility behavior.
tldr: This paper develops a single-loop primal-dual constraint extrapolation method (PD-ConEx) for solving monotone variational inequalities with semi-infinite constraints.
motivation: Semi-infinite constraints require feasibility over infinitely many indices, making projection onto the full feasible region intractable, yet such models underpin robust optimization, distributionally robust learning, and generalized Nash equilibrium problems.
method: PD-ConEx jointly updates primal variables, Lagrange multipliers, and worst-case constraint indices using first-order information, linearization, extrapolation, and projections onto simple sets, with an adaptive smooth variant for improved VI-gap and feasibility guarantees.
result: The authors prove convergence rates for smooth and nonsmooth regimes, showing dependence on strong monotonicity and strong concavity of the index block, and demonstrate optimality and feasibility behavior on robust quadratic and distributionally robust learning experiments.
conclusion: The framework unifies several constrained saddle-point and robust optimization settings and provides practical first-order algorithms with theoretical guarantees, though it is entirely a classical optimization contribution.

title: When Are Nesterov Trajectories Eventually Locally Minimizing?
authors: Stephen Wright Peyman Morteza
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the variational characterization of Nesterov's celebrated method and study when Nesterov trajectories are eventually locally minimizing in a variational sense, a notion that we define precisely. We show that this question is equivalent to the nonnegativity of an associated Schr\"odinger operator acting on variations of the trajectory. For power objectives of the form \[ f(x)={p}\|x\|^p \] (where [MATH] denotes the Euclidean norm), we give a complete characterization: Among all exponents [MATH], the Nesterov trajectory with non-zero initial position is eventually locally minimizing if and only if [MATH]. We further interpret this exceptional exponent through the stability theory of semilinear elliptic equations.
tldr: The paper characterizes when Nesterov's accelerated gradient trajectories are eventually locally minimizing in a variational sense, linking this to nonnegativity of an associated Schrödinger operator and showing that for power objectives this holds only at one exceptional exponent.
motivation: Nesterov's method admits a variational (Bregman/integral) characterization, but it is unclear when the resulting trajectories are genuine local minimizers of the variational objective rather than merely critical points.
method: The authors define eventual local minimality precisely, reformulate the second-variation condition as nonnegativity of a Schrödinger-type operator acting on trajectory variations, and analyze power objectives f(x)=p||x||^p, invoking stability theory of semilinear elliptic equations.
result: A complete characterization is obtained: among all exponents p, Nesterov trajectories with nonzero initial position are eventually locally minimizing if and only if p takes one exceptional value, which is interpreted via semilinear elliptic stability theory.
conclusion: The work clarifies the variational geometry of accelerated gradient methods and identifies a sharp threshold exponent, connecting optimization dynamics to spectral/stability properties of Schrödinger operators.

title: Pinching Antenna And Relay Assisted Joint Indoor Outdoor Noma Communications With Swipt
authors: Amit Agarwal, Susmita Sain, Keshav Singh, Sudip Biswas
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates physical layer security in waveguide-based pinching antenna systems with a mobile eavesdropper. Assuming perfect knowledge of the legitimate user's location and only statistical information about the eavesdropper's position, the ergodic secrecy rate is analyzed under Gaussian and practical finite-alphabet signaling. Since the exact ergodic secrecy rate does not admit a tractable closed-form expression, a closed-form analytical upper bound is derived using Jensen's inequality. The resulting expression serves as an efficient objective for antenna position optimization without requiring exhaustive Monte Carlo simulations. Numerical results verify the tightness of the proposed upper bound and show that the optimized antenna position closely matches the optimum obtained from Monte Carlo optimization. Furthermore, practical finite-alphabet signaling is shown to exhibit secrecy-rate saturation at high SNR, identifying an effective operating SNR region. Although the antenna position is optimized using the Gaussian-based upper bound, it remains effective for practical signaling.
tldr: The paper analyzes ergodic secrecy rate for waveguide-based pinching antenna systems with a mobile eavesdropper and optimizes antenna position using a closed-form upper bound.
motivation: Physical layer security in emerging pinching-antenna wireless systems is important when eavesdropper location is only statistically known and finite-alphabet signaling is used.
method: It derives a Jensen-based closed-form upper bound on ergodic secrecy rate under Gaussian and finite-alphabet signaling, then uses this bound as an optimization objective for antenna positioning and validates it numerically against Monte Carlo results.
result: The upper bound is tight, optimized antenna positions closely match Monte Carlo optima, and finite-alphabet signaling shows secrecy-rate saturation at high SNR, defining an effective operating region.
conclusion: The proposed bound enables efficient antenna-position optimization for secrecy in pinching-antenna systems and remains effective under practical finite-alphabet signaling.

title: Optimization-based Cell Average Limiters As Metric Projections: Constrained Evolution And Convergence Analysis For Convection-diffusion Equations
authors: Seungmin Lee, Sanghyun Lee, Chen Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The optimization-based cell average limiter enforces global conservation and bounds, and has been successfully applied to discontinuous Galerkin (DG) discretizations of a wide range of nonlinear systems, from phase-field models to the compressible Navier-Stokes equations. In this paper, taking the heat and convection-diffusion equations as prototypes, we analyze the convergence of the scheme resulting from cell average limiting. Encoding conservation and admissibility in a differential inclusion identifies the limiter as a backward Euler proximal step in a Lie splitting of the constrained evolution. This proximal step is the metric projection onto the convex admissible set, and we prove that it is nonexpansive and stable in the [MATH] norm, and that it does not increase the total variation of the cell averages. Combined with the standard error analysis, nonexpansiveness yields an [MATH] estimate for implicit Euler time stepping with DG discretization of polynomial degree [MATH] under a reverse CFL condition, together with an unconditional [MATH] estimate. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates and the enforcement of the bounds.
tldr: This paper analyzes optimization-based cell average limiters for discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of convection-diffusion equations, interpreting the limiter as a metric projection in a constrained evolution scheme.
motivation: The cell average limiter is widely used to enforce conservation and admissibility in DG methods, but its convergence properties require a rigorous theoretical foundation.
method: The authors formulate conservation and admissibility as a differential inclusion, identify the limiter as a backward Euler proximal step within a Lie splitting, and prove nonexpansiveness, stability, and total-variation non-increase of the metric projection.
result: Combining the projection properties with standard error analysis yields L2 error estimates for implicit Euler DG time stepping under a reverse CFL condition, along with an unconditional estimate, confirmed by numerical experiments.
conclusion: The metric-projection perspective provides a convergence framework for optimization-based cell average limiters in convection-diffusion DG schemes.

title: Ambient Chain-Relation Reduction In Contracting Controlled Skew-Product Semiflows
authors: Robert Vrabel
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The qualitative dynamics of nonautonomous differential equations is often studied through cocycles and skew-product semiflows over a driving base. We develop a chain-recurrence reduction principle for systems admitting an equivariant attracting section and uniform asymptotic tracking. The abstract theorem determines the complete chain-attainability relation in the ambient phase space: chains may start off the attracting section, but every attainable target lies on it and is selected solely by the factor semiflow. Applied to contracting controlled skew-product semiflows, this gives exact descriptions of the chain recurrent set, chain components, Conley order, compact strictly invariant sets, attractors, basins, and dual repellers. A weighted-supremum transverse gauge yields a complete Lyapunov function for the full semiflow while preserving the recurrent values of the base. The differential hypotheses are verified through subadditive fiber-derivative growth and averaged moving-metric logarithmic norms, allowing transient expansion and non-unique ergodicity. Quantitative persistence is established for finite-window maps and smooth vector-field perturbations. The results provide a unified framework for chain recurrence, Lyapunov structure, and attractor--repeller geometry in contracting nonautonomous dynamics.
tldr: The paper develops a chain-recurrence reduction principle for nonautonomous skew-product semiflows admitting an equivariant attracting section, with applications to contracting controlled skew-product flows.
motivation: Qualitative dynamics of nonautonomous differential equations are typically studied via cocycles and skew-product semiflows, but a systematic reduction of chain recurrence to the driving base was lacking.
method: An abstract chain-recurrence reduction theorem is proven under uniform asymptotic tracking and transverse gauge conditions, with differential hypotheses verified via subadditive fiber-derivative growth and averaged moving-metric logarithmic norms.
result: Exact descriptions of chain recurrent sets, Conley order, attractors, basins, and dual repellers are obtained, together with a complete Lyapunov function preserving base recurrent values and quantitative persistence bounds.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for chain recurrence, Lyapunov structure, and attractor-repeller geometry in contracting nonautonomous dynamics, but has no connection to quantum information science.

title: Ordinary Algebras Of Complex-valued Functions
authors: Karim Boulabiar
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A classical theorem due to Gleason, Kahane, and Zelazko states that every complex unital Banach algebra is ordinary, meaning that any linear functional mapping elements into their spectrum is a character. While Roitman and Sternfeld extended this property to algebras with bounded spectra-showing in particular that the algebra C(X) of continuous functions is ordinary when X is pseudocompact-the general case of C(X) for arbitrary topological spaces X appears to be open, as we could not locate any reference in this direction. In this paper, we show that the pseudocompactness condition is unnecessary, that is, C(X) is ordinary for every topological space X. This fact is obtained as a consequence of a more general result characterizing positive characters on a purely algebraic generalization of unital C*-algebras, which we introduce under the name of AC*-algebras. As applications, we obtain two necessary and sufficient conditions for a Tychonoff space X to be realcompact in terms of 1-evaluating linear functionals on C(X) and their continuity with respect to the compact-open topology. Finally, we establish a Banach--Stone type theorem showing that two realcompact spaces X and Y are homeomorphic if and only if C(X) and C(Y) are linearly isomorphic via a map that preserves invertibility.
tldr: The paper proves that the algebra C(X) of continuous complex-valued functions is ordinary for every topological space X, generalizing the Gleason-Kahane-Zelazko theorem and related results.
motivation: The ordinary property of C(X) was known for pseudocompact X via Roitman and Sternfeld, but the general case for arbitrary topological spaces was open; the author removes the pseudocompactness assumption.
method: The proof introduces a purely algebraic generalization of unital C*-algebras called AC*-algebras and characterizes positive characters on them, then applies this characterization to C(X).
result: It is shown that C(X) is ordinary for every topological space X, and two necessary and sufficient conditions for a Tychonoff space to be realcompact are obtained in terms of 1-evaluating functionals and compact-open continuity; a Banach-Stone type theorem for realcompact spaces is also established.
conclusion: The work settles the open problem on ordinary algebras of continuous functions and provides applications to realcompactness and Banach-Stone-type classification.

title: A Structure Theorem For Multiple Correlation Sequences On Nilsystems
authors: Or Shalom
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, the author refuted several conjectures about the vanishing of multiple correlation sequences. The goal of this paper is to provide a counterpart for the conjectures of Frantzikinakis--Kuca and of Leibman. The significance of this manuscript is twofold: firstly, we provide a structure theorem for multiple correlation sequences on nilsystems along arithmetic progressions (in the sense of Frantzikinakis--Kuca), and a corresponding structure theorem for polynomial orbits of subnilmanifolds in connected nilmanifolds (in the sense of Leibman). Secondly, we identify null generalized nilsequences, as a notion of smallness, which provides a structured counterpart for null sequences. In particular, in the special case of ergodic nilsystems, we answer positively a question of Frantzikinakis on the structure of multiple correlation sequences.
tldr: The paper proves structure theorems for multiple correlation sequences on nilsystems along arithmetic progressions, together with a structure theorem for polynomial orbits of subnilmanifolds, and introduces null generalized nilsequences as a notion of smallness.
motivation: Following the author's recent refutation of several conjectures on the vanishing of multiple correlation sequences, this work aims to supply the positive counterpart to conjectures of Frantzikinakis–Kuca and of Leibman.
method: Ergodic-theoretic and nilmanifold-based analysis: structure theorems for correlation sequences along arithmetic progressions on nilsystems and for polynomial orbits of subnilmanifolds in connected nilmanifolds, plus the definition of null generalized nilsequences.
result: A structure theorem for multiple correlation sequences on nilsystems is established, null generalized nilsequences are identified as a structured smallness notion, and Frantzikinakis's question on the structure of multiple correlation sequences is answered positively in the ergodic nilsystem case.
conclusion: The results provide a structured counterpart to null sequences and resolve open structural questions in the ergodic theory of nilsystems, but lie entirely outside quantum information science.

title: The Closed Convex Hull Of All Associative Copulas Is A Z-set In The Family Of All Bivariate Schur Concave Copulas, And Related Results
authors: Manuel \'ubeda-Flores Wolfgang Trutschnig
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Very recently, Problem 2.5 stated by Mesiar and Sarkoci in and originally formulated by Durante was answered in the negative by eliga . The author showed that the closed convex hull of all bivariate associative copulas is a proper subset of the family of all Schur concave copulas, and even computed the exact uniform distance of his counterexamples to the closed convex hull (so that the Hausdorff distance between the two families is at least [MATH]). Using the fact that every bivariate associative copula can be represented as a (finite or countably infinite) ordinal sum of Archimedean copulas and the minimum copula [MATH], and working with the Markov kernels of Archimedean copulas, we first give an alternative, simple proof of the strict inclusion. We do so by showing that convex combinations of associative copulas can assign only very little mass to certain line segments parallel to the main diagonal, a result we later extend to so-called chains and staircases. Building on the first observation, we then go one step further and show that, from a topological perspective, the closed convex hull of all associative copulas is a very small subset of the Schur concave family, namely a so-called [MATH]-set, and that the family of associative copulas is, in turn, a [MATH]-set in its closed convex hull.
tldr: The paper proves topological smallness results for the closed convex hull of bivariate associative copulas within the family of Schur concave copulas.
motivation: It addresses a problem on whether the closed convex hull of associative copulas equals the family of Schur concave copulas, and strengthens the negative answer with topological notions.
method: It uses the ordinal-sum representation of associative copulas, Markov kernels of Archimedean copulas, and mass estimates on diagonal-parallel line segments, chains, and staircases.
result: The closed convex hull of associative copulas is shown to be a Z-set in the family of bivariate Schur concave copulas, and the family of associative copulas is a Z-set in its closed convex hull.
conclusion: The result establishes a strong topological separation between associative copulas and Schur concave copulas, going beyond strict inclusion.

title: Weak Mixing And Non-recurrence Along Finitely Generated Multiplicative Semigroups Of $\mathbb N$
authors: Zhuowei Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a finite nonempty set of primes, and let [MATH] be the multiplicative semigroup that they generate. We prove that there are an invertible weakly mixing measure-preserving transformation [MATH] and a set [MATH] of positive measure such that [MATH] for every [MATH]. This gives a negative answer to Bergelson's 1996 question concerning recurrence along [MATH], and applies to every finitely generated multiplicative semigroup of positive integers. More generally, we give a sufficient condition for weakly mixing non-recurrence based on divisibility properties and separation by finitely many rotations of the circle. This criterion also applies to an infinitely generated multiplicative semigroup not contained in any [MATH] with [MATH] finite.
tldr: The paper constructs an invertible weakly mixing measure-preserving transformation that fails to recur along finitely generated multiplicative semigroups of primes, answering Bergelson's 1996 question negatively.
motivation: Bergelson asked in 1996 whether weak mixing implies recurrence along the multiplicative semigroup generated by a finite set of primes; this work resolves that question in the negative and characterizes when such non-recurrence can occur.
method: The author builds measure-preserving transformations on suitable probability spaces, using divisibility structure and separation of orbits by finitely many circle rotations to establish a general sufficient criterion for weakly mixing non-recurrence.
result: For every finite set of primes there exist an invertible weakly mixing transformation and a positive-measure set whose points never return under the semigroup action; the criterion extends to certain infinitely generated semigroups not contained in any finitely generated sub-semigroup.
conclusion: Weak mixing does not guarantee recurrence along multiplicative semigroups, and the divisibility-based rotation-separation mechanism delineates a broad class of non-recurring weakly mixing systems.

title: Optimal Voting: Beyond A Utilitarian View
authors: Nicholas Mattei Ben Armstrong
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A common measure of the quality of a voting rule is the social welfare of the alternatives it elects. Prior work shows that, when voter utilities are drawn from a neutral distribution, expected utilitarian welfare is maximized by a positional scoring rule. We extend this approach to the power mean family of welfare functions, which includes utilitarian, Nash, and egalitarian welfare as special cases. We show that, across the power mean family, a deterministic positional scoring rule (PSR) is asymptotically optimal for expected social welfare among all social choice functions and we characterize this rule for a broad class of utility distributions. We further show that, among randomized PSRs, plurality uniquely maximizes expected social welfare for all power means. Experimentally, we find that optimal score vectors often yield substantially higher welfare than canonical score vectors. On highly structured utility distributions, optimal score vectors take on novel shapes unlike existing canonical score vectors, highlighting open questions for future analysis.
tldr: The paper extends social welfare analysis of voting rules to the power mean family and shows deterministic positional scoring rules are asymptotically optimal for expected social welfare under neutral utility distributions.
motivation: Prior work establishes that positional scoring rules maximize expected utilitarian welfare when utilities are drawn from neutral distributions. This paper asks whether that conclusion extends beyond utilitarianism to Nash, egalitarian, and other power-mean welfare functions.
method: The authors analyze expected social welfare over the power mean family for deterministic and randomized social choice functions, characterize optimal positional scoring rules for broad utility distributions, and conduct experiments comparing optimal and canonical score vectors.
result: A deterministic positional scoring rule is asymptotically optimal across the power mean family, plurality uniquely maximizes expected social welfare among randomized positional scoring rules, and optimal score vectors can differ substantially from canonical ones and take novel shapes on structured distributions.
conclusion: The results generalize welfare-optimal voting beyond utilitarian social welfare and highlight open questions about optimal score vectors under structured utility distributions.

title: From Hype To Roi: An Economic Model For Llm Adoption In Information Systems And Security Operations
authors: Pellegrino Casoria, Andrea Araldo, Rosario Patan\`e, Simon Pietro Romano
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) promise significant efficiency gains across information-intensive operations by automating repetitive language-based tasks. However, adoption decisions remain largely opportunistic, as organizations struggle to move from pilots to sustainable industrialization. Without systematic economic frameworks, practitioners cannot assess whether LLM investments create value in a given context. This paper develops a general economic model to support informed LLM adoption decisions in operational information systems. Facing high uncertainty, we represent parameters as random variables centered on authoritative benchmarks, and evaluate the model by Monte Carlo simulation across pessimistic-to-optimistic assumptions on LLM efficiency. The ROI distributions show the probability of profitability and the Value at Risk for each configuration, together with a sensitivity analysis of its main drivers. As a first instantiation, we apply the model to Security Operations Centers (SOCs), mapping workflows onto established standards to identify tasks suited to LLM augmentation. The model balances productivity gains, driven by alert volume, analyst effort, and LLM efficiency, against operational costs, including inference, infrastructure, and error remediation, covering both cloud API and self-hosted deployments. Results show that adoption economics are context-dependent, and that automation is an exploitable lever, gated by accuracy, while the cost of errors and the model's price are secondary. Across the analyzed models and prices, most configurations are unprofitable, with profitability limited to high-accuracy, low-uncertainty deployments. The model gives organizations a quantitative basis for evidence-based adoption decisions, by locating the boundary between profit and loss, and the loss risked beyond it.
tldr: The paper builds a Monte Carlo-based economic model (ROI distributions, Value at Risk, sensitivity analysis) to decide whether adopting LLMs pays off in operational information systems, instantiated for Security Operations Centers.
motivation: Organizations adopt LLMs opportunistically without systematic economic frameworks, so practitioners lack a quantitative way to tell whether an LLM investment creates value in a given operational context.
method: Parameters are treated as random variables centered on authoritative benchmarks, and the model is evaluated by Monte Carlo simulation over pessimistic-to-optimistic assumptions on LLM efficiency, balancing productivity gains against inference, infrastructure, and error-remediation costs for cloud and self-hosted deployments.
result: Adoption economics are strongly context-dependent: automation is an exploitable lever gated by accuracy, while error cost and model price are secondary; across analyzed models and prices most configurations are unprofitable, with profitability confined to high-accuracy, low-uncertainty deployments.
conclusion: The model gives organizations a quantitative boundary between profit and loss, plus the loss risked beyond it, enabling evidence-based LLM adoption decisions in information systems and security operations.

title: Combinatorial Lock For Trojan-Resilient Ai Engines Via Hash-Assisted Spectral Filtering
authors: Soumita Chatterjee, Sudip Ghosh, Tamal Ghosh, Bhargab B. Bhattacharya, Hafizur Rahaman
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-trigger backdoor attacks, in which heterogeneous trigger mechanisms (e.g., patch, blend, warping, and the latent-domain Spy-Watermark) coexist within a single poisoned model, cannot be addressed by existing shortcut-based defenses that assume a single, static attack mechanism. Current multi-trigger remedies (BU+FT, BU+ANP, and BU+ABL) rely on backdoor unlearning, which incurs high training costs and loses effectiveness at low poisoning ratios. This paper proposes Combinatorial Lock, a training-free, reference-calibrated defense that reduces multi-trigger identification to a combinatorial problem over binary activation signatures. This formulation is the key novelty: it yields a multi-trigger defense that is training-free, trigger-oblivious, and directly implementable in hardware, since its decision rules can be evaluated with integer and logic operations. The framework combines anomaly-gated spectral scrubbing, which removes the malicious subspace only from inputs identified as anomalous, with a hash-compressed combinatorial signature verified by an ensemble of detection experts, including a compound-attack-aware expert for multi-trigger inputs. A joint threshold-shrinkage search identifies an operating point ([MATH] at the 97.1st percentile, [MATH]) that reduces the attack success rate (ASR) to as low as 0.1% while preserving 97.8% clean accuracy. Evaluation on six models (ResNet18, VGG16, MobileNet, AlexNet, ViT-Small, ViT-Base) shows strong generalization: near-100% ASR drops to single digits across poisoning rates of 1-10% and 1-9 simultaneous triggers, with only gradual degradation in clean accuracy. ASIC and FPGA implementations confirm practicality, adding a consistent 19-20% latency overhead across all evaluated architectures and establishing Combinatorial Lock as a hardware-native approach to multi-trigger backdoor mitigation.
tldr: Combinatorial Lock is a training-free, hardware-implementable defense against multi-trigger backdoor attacks in deep neural networks, using anomaly-gated spectral scrubbing and hash-compressed combinatorial activation signatures.
motivation: Existing defenses against backdoor poisoning assume a single static trigger mechanism and rely on costly backdoor unlearning that fails at low poisoning ratios, leaving multi-trigger attacks unaddressed.
method: The authors recast multi-trigger identification as a combinatorial problem over binary activation signatures, combining anomaly-gated spectral scrubbing of the malicious subspace with a hash-compressed signature verified by an ensemble of detection experts, tuned via joint threshold-shrinkage search and implemented in ASIC/FPGA.
result: Across six CNN and ViT architectures, attack success rates drop from near-100% to as low as 0.1% at 1-10% poisoning and 1-9 simultaneous triggers, while clean accuracy stays at 97.8%, with only 19-20% latency overhead in hardware.
conclusion: The work establishes a hardware-native, trigger-oblivious defense for multi-trigger backdoors, but it concerns classical machine learning security and VLSI design rather than any quantum information, thermodynamic, network, or hybrid-platform topic.

title: VulDec: Vulnerability Detection In Binaries Via Neural Decompilation
authors: Francesco Crescenzo Grasso, Pietro Liguori, Roberto Natella, Domenico Cotroneo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated vulnerability detection in binary executables is challenging due to the lack of source code and the limited semantic information available at the assembly level. Despite significant progress in machine-learning-based code analysis, the field still lacks methodologies and large, high-quality datasets that provide vulnerable code jointly at assembly- and source-level with precise vulnerability labels. To address this gap, we introduce VulDec, consisting of (i) a new large-scale, carefully curated dataset aligning real-world Assembly-C function pairs with detailed CWE annotations across multiple architectures, and (ii) the first end-to-end framework that leverages neural decompilation for binary vulnerability detection. Tuned LLM-based neural decompilers trained on our dataset achieve strong source-level recovery across architectures (Edit Similarity of approximately 56%, BLEU-4 of approximately 43%), while our tuned LLM-based detectors reach a macro F1-score of 0.61 on an in-distribution realistic test set (3% vulnerability rate). Our findings provide evidence that neural decompilation offers a powerful alternative to conventional low-level binary representations, facilitating robust binary vulnerability detection.
tldr: VulDec introduces a large-scale Assembly-C dataset and an end-to-end neural-decompilation pipeline for binary vulnerability detection using tuned LLMs.
motivation: Binary vulnerability detection is difficult because source code is unavailable and assembly-level semantics are limited, and the field lacks high-quality datasets aligning assembly and source code with precise vulnerability labels.
method: The authors build a curated dataset of real-world Assembly-C function pairs with CWE annotations across architectures, then tune LLM-based neural decompilers and LLM-based vulnerability detectors on this data.
result: The tuned decompilers achieve about 56% Edit Similarity and 43% BLEU-4, while the tuned detectors reach a macro F1-score of 0.61 on a realistic in-distribution test set with a 3% vulnerability rate.
conclusion: Neural decompilation is presented as a powerful alternative to conventional low-level binary representations for robust binary vulnerability detection.

title: Enhancing LLM-Based Vulnerability Detection Via Representation-Aware Logical Ensemble
authors: Francesco Crescenzo Grasso, Pietro Liguori, Roberto Natella, Domenico Cotroneo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated vulnerability detection in C source code is a long-standing challenge, as traditional static analysis tools often trade precision for scalability and struggle with complex vulnerability patterns. Recently, large language models (LLMs) have shown promising results; yet, most approaches rely on a single code representation, implicitly assuming uniform suitability across vulnerability types. In this work, we systematically study LLM-based vulnerability detection under multiple code representations, including raw source code, Abstract Syntax Trees (AST), and Control Flow Graphs (CFG). Through extensive empirical analysis, we show that different representations exhibit complementary strengths, with specific views being more effective for particular classes of vulnerabilities. Building on these findings, we propose a Representation-Aware Logical Ensemble (RALE) that integrates LLMs trained on different code representations through explicit logical rules and majority voting. While single-representation models achieve up to 73% F1-score, our integrated approach reaches 78% F1-score, with commensurate gains in accuracy, precision, and recall, consistently outperforming individual models. These results highlight the importance of explicitly leveraging complementary code representations when combining LLMs for effective vulnerability detection.
tldr: The paper studies LLM-based vulnerability detection in C source code across multiple code representations (raw source, AST, CFG) and proposes a representation-aware logical ensemble that combines them via logical rules and majority voting.
motivation: Static analysis tools trade precision for scalability and miss complex vulnerability patterns, while existing LLM approaches assume a single code representation is uniformly suitable across vulnerability classes.
method: Empirically compares LLM detectors operating on raw source code, Abstract Syntax Trees, and Control Flow Graphs, then integrates their predictions through explicit logical rules plus majority voting (RALE).
result: Individual representation-specific models reach up to 73% F1, while the ensemble reaches 78% F1 with consistent gains in accuracy, precision, and recall over any single model.
conclusion: Explicitly exploiting complementary code representations improves LLM-based vulnerability detection, arguing against the one-representation-fits-all assumption.

title: The Conditional Value Of Costly Information In Collective-Risk Dilemmas
authors: Elias Fern\'andez Domingos, Genki Ichinose, Wakaba Tateishi, Tom Lenaerts
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many high-stakes collective problems, e.g., climate mitigation and pandemic response, share a structure in which risk materializes unless a group threshold is met. This threshold is often uncertain, but uncertainty can be reduced at a cost. We study this information cost tradeoff in an evolutionary game theoretic model of social learning in the collective-risk dilemma, where individuals must cooperate to reach a possibly uncertain threshold to prevent collective loss. Individuals may pay a fixed cost to observe the threshold's true value and condition their cooperation on it. Across four threshold priors, we characterize risk levels at which cooperative equilibria emerge and show that low cost information increases group success. However, this effect is reversed at higher costs. We define a private and show that information is worth buying only when it is considerably cheaper than contributing. When purchased information is shared with the group, the cooperative tipping point shifts to lower risk levels. Despite bearing a private cost, above this tipping point buyers earn more in expectation than information free-riders. We then study these dynamics when information diffuses through a network, allowing nodes to relay it. Although fewer individuals pay for information, relaying increases group success, and noisy relaying does not reduce it. By contrast, false information does, especially when it originates at the hubs of heterogeneous networks, and large attacks can bring collective action close to collapse. Buyers act as a firewall against disinformation, confining it to source neighbourhoods, and once disinformation sources are removed, the population recovers. The value of costly information thus depends on its price, the level of risk, and how it is shared, and, in our setting, the effort of acquiring it also protects the population against disinformation.
tldr: The paper models costly threshold information acquisition and sharing in collective-risk dilemmas using evolutionary game theory and network diffusion.
motivation: Many collective-action problems involve uncertain thresholds, so understanding when costly information about the threshold promotes cooperation is important.
method: An evolutionary game-theoretic model of social learning is used, where individuals may pay to observe the true threshold and condition cooperation on it, including cases with information sharing and network diffusion.
result: Low-cost information improves group success, but high costs reverse this; sharing shifts tipping points, buyers can outperform free-riders above a threshold, and relaying helps while false information—especially from network hubs—can undermine collective action.
conclusion: The value of costly information depends on price, risk level, and sharing structure, and information acquisition can also act as a firewall against disinformation.

title: Some New Criteria For The Uniqueness Of Limit Cycles In Rayleigh--Lienard Systems
authors: Hebai Chen, Dongmei Xiao, Rui Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33114v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, new uniqueness criteria for Rayleigh--Li\'enard systems with damping of positive odd degree in the velocity are established. Under suitable conditions, any limit cycle is unique and hyperbolic, with its stability determined by the damping signs. Neither symmetry nor monotonicity of the damping and restoring functions is required. Changes of variables and time yield further criteria for generalized Kukles systems. Applications to three polynomial families yield uniqueness and nonexistence results. In particular, we resolve an open uniqueness problem for a hybrid van der Pol--Rayleigh oscillator left open by Chen et al. (Phys. D, 2021). We also give an alternative uniqueness proof for a system with homogeneous components and obtain uniqueness and nonexistence results for a modified hybrid van der Pol--Rayleigh oscillator.
tldr: The paper establishes new uniqueness criteria for limit cycles in Rayleigh-Liénard systems and applies them to polynomial oscillator families.
motivation: Uniqueness and hyperbolicity of limit cycles are central problems in nonlinear dynamical systems, with open cases remaining for certain hybrid van der Pol–Rayleigh oscillators.
method: The authors derive analytic criteria for Rayleigh-Liénard systems with odd-degree damping, using changes of variables and time to extend results to generalized Kukles systems.
result: They obtain uniqueness, hyperbolicity, stability, and nonexistence results, resolving an open uniqueness problem for a hybrid van der Pol–Rayleigh oscillator and providing an alternative proof for a homogeneous-component system.
conclusion: The work advances the mathematical theory of limit cycles in planar dynamical systems but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optimal Non-Homogeneous Improvements Of The Anisotropic Hardy Inequality
authors: Giuseppina Di Blasio, Giovanni Pisante, Georgios Psaradakis
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Hardy inequality associated with a strongly convex Finsler norm [MATH] on [MATH] and we study its optimal non-homogeneous improvements in the whole range [MATH]. We show that the anisotropic Hardy difference controls a weighted critical Sobolev norm when [MATH], proving in each regime that the logarithmic weights appear with the optimal exponents. In the borderline case [MATH] this extends to general functions the optimal exponent previously known only for anisotropically radial functions. The proofs rely on a common ground-state reduction, combined with a splitting into an [MATH]-radial and a mean-free part for [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves optimal non-homogeneous improvements of an anisotropic Hardy inequality associated with a strongly convex Finsler norm.
motivation: The authors aim to extend optimal Hardy-inequality improvements, including logarithmic-weight exponents, across the full parameter range and to general functions in the borderline case.
method: The proofs use a common ground-state reduction and split functions into an anisotropic radial part and a mean-free part.
result: The anisotropic Hardy difference is shown to control a weighted critical Sobolev norm in each regime, with optimal logarithmic-weight exponents, including a borderline extension beyond anisotropically radial functions.
conclusion: The work establishes sharp anisotropic Hardy inequalities and provides a unified approach to optimal non-homogeneous improvements.

title: Targeting Interventions For Volatility Reduction In Network Systems - Part I: Idiosyncratic Shocks
authors: Luca Damonte, Leonardo Cianfanelli, Giacomo Como, Fabio Fagnani
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study optimal intervention design problems aimed at minimizing the aggregate volatility in network systems. We consider linear network equilibrium models arising in network games, production networks, and opinion dynamics, where exogenous shocks hitting a few nodes can propagate through the network and cause detrimental systemic effects. Focusing on idiosyncratic shocks, we first identify a general network centrality measure that determines the amplification factor of the variance of each node's shock to the aggregate system volatility, and show that, in relevant special cases, it reduces to Katz-Bonacich, cycle, and concentration centralities. We then consider a system planner who can attenuate the shocks on the nodes, subject to a budget constraint, so as to minimize the aggregate volatility. We solve this problem analytically and show that its solution has a water-filling-type structure: for low budget, the intervention is concentrated on the node(s) maximizing a quantity {\omega}_i that combines the shock's variance, the node's centrality, and the intervention cost; as the budget increases, more and more nodes are targeted, and for sufficiently large budget every node with {\omega}_i > 0 receives an intervention proportional to {\omega}_i. Finally, we study a robust version of the problem, where the planner minimizes the volatility against the worst-case vector of shock variances chosen by an adversary within a given budget. We solve this min-max problem analytically and show that its solution also has a water-filling-type structure, with the ratio between the node's centrality and the square root of the adversarial cost playing the role of {\omega}_i.
tldr: The paper derives optimal budget-constrained intervention strategies for reducing aggregate volatility in linear network equilibrium models subject to idiosyncratic shocks.
motivation: Exogenous shocks hitting a few nodes in network games, production networks, or opinion dynamics can propagate and amplify into systemic volatility, so a planner needs principled ways to decide where to intervene under limited budget.
method: The authors identify a network centrality measure governing how each node's shock variance is amplified into aggregate volatility, then analytically solve a budget-constrained minimization and a robust min-max version against adversarial shock variances.
result: Both problems admit water-filling-type solutions: for small budgets interventions concentrate on the node maximizing a composite weight of shock variance, centrality, and cost, and as the budget grows targets expand until all nodes with positive weight receive proportional intervention.
conclusion: The framework provides closed-form, interpretable intervention rules for volatility reduction in networked systems, unifying Katz-Bonacich, cycle, and concentration centralities as special cases.

title: Optimizing Physical Neural Networks Through Device Variable Selection
authors: Sjoerd van Den Belt, Manuel Escudero, Mohamadreza Zolfagharinejad, Wilfred G. van der Wiel, Nikolaos Alachiotis
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physical neural networks (PNNs) leverage device physics in electronics, optics, and related domains to enable energy-efficient neural networks. Broken-isomorphism PNNs replace linear operations with multivariate physical transformations, modifying how input signals are mapped to device variables. We exploit network architectures emerging from these mappings by treating the routing between signals and input variables of physical devices as trainable parameters. This approach expands device-level tunability of the physical transformations while, at the system level, demonstrating improved expressivity of PNNs with negligible additional inference overhead. This discrete routing is optimized by training a categorical distribution using Gumbel-Softmax reparametrization. We evaluate this approach using experimentally calibrated differentiable models of multivariate electronic RNPUs for MNIST and CIFAR-10 classification. Using variable selection, we improve the MNIST classification accuracy for a small CNN model from 94.5% to 96.9% and the accuracy of CIFAR-10 from 62.8% to 68.0%. Our method uniquely leverages the induced biases of broken-isomorphism PNN architectures, paving the way towards more efficient physics-based neural network inference.
tldr: The paper proposes trainable discrete routing between signals and physical device variables in broken-isomorphism physical neural networks, optimized via Gumbel-Softmax, to improve classification accuracy with negligible inference overhead.
motivation: Physical neural networks aim to exploit device physics for energy-efficient computation, but their broken-isomorphism architectures introduce multivariate physical transformations whose routing structure is not fully exploited.
