method: The authors treat the routing between input signals and device variables as trainable categorical parameters and optimize them with Gumbel-Softmax reparameterization, evaluated on experimentally calibrated differentiable models of multivariate electronic RNPUs for MNIST and CIFAR-10.
result: Variable selection improves MNIST accuracy from 94.5% to 96.9% and CIFAR-10 accuracy from 62.8% to 68.0% for a small CNN.
conclusion: The approach leverages induced biases of broken-isomorphism PNN architectures and offers a path toward more efficient physics-based neural network inference.

title: Pacifo: An Efficient Fully Homomorphic Encryption-based Lightweight ResNet For Trustworthy Machine Learning As A Service
authors: Yang Li, Gang He, Ruichen Zhang, Guangyuan Liu, Yinqiu Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS) has become a popular paradigm for deploying AI applications. However, it raises significant privacy concerns that the raw client data needs to be uploaded to the server for inference services. Private inference using Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) offers a solution by allowing computations directly on encrypted data, with only the final results decrypted on a client side. However, current practical implementations still suffer from large computational overhead and high latency due to the cost of FHE operations. In this paper, we propose Pacifo, a framework that adapts customized fine-tuning strategies to efficiently evaluate the ResNet20 model in the context of FHE. Specifically, Pacifo introduces a public-private layer partitioning scheme and an efficient ReLU approximation, significantly reducing the number of private layers and costly FHE operations during inference. It also offers flexible security configurations to accommodate varying client privacy requirements. Compared to state-of-the-art FHE implementations of ResNet20, Pacifo achieves a speedup of [MATH] in runtime while effectively preserving [MATH] of the original plaintext model accuracy across downstream tasks. Pacifo is open-sourced at [URL].
tldr: Pacifo is a fully homomorphic encryption-based framework that fine-tunes and partitions ResNet20 to enable efficient privacy-preserving inference for machine-learning-as-a-service.
motivation: MLaaS requires clients to upload raw data, creating privacy risks; fully homomorphic encryption enables inference on encrypted data but suffers from high computational overhead and latency.
method: The paper proposes public-private layer partitioning, an efficient ReLU approximation, and flexible security configurations to reduce the number of private layers and costly FHE operations during ResNet20 inference.
result: Compared with state-of-the-art FHE implementations of ResNet20, Pacifo achieves a significant runtime speedup while preserving most of the original plaintext model accuracy across downstream tasks.
conclusion: Pacifo demonstrates that customized fine-tuning and layer partitioning can make FHE-based private inference for ResNet models more practical, though the work is focused on applied privacy-preserving machine learning rather than quantum information science.

title: Who Verifies The Verifiers? Accountable Semantic Consensus For AI-Mediated Web Information Verification
authors: Yanna Jiang, Mingyuan Li, Xu Wang, Guangsheng Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly decide whether Web evidence supports online claims, often by voting over several assessors whose errors are presumed independent and benign. On the open Web, retrieved pages can steer the assessors that read them, and assessors from one model family fail together. We prove that even for independent assessors whose every output sequence is possible on both valid and invalid claims, any protocol that decides only from their outputs and always reaches an agreed verdict never rejects invalid claims or rejects valid ones with positive probability. We present Astral, which pins all assessors to one committed snapshot of the Web evidence. With up to f assessors faulty, Astral accepts a verdict only when 2f+1 assessors attest to it above a confidence threshold and no signed challenge stands. On five public benchmarks with two of seven assessors adversarial, Astral lowers pooled attack success to 21.5-53.1%, against 54.7-77.8% for majority voting. The cost is coverage, as without attack 16.0-61.7% of claims receive a binary verdict and the rest are disputed for audit. Our code runs at [URL].
tldr: The paper proves an impossibility result for output-only consensus protocols over LLM assessors verifying web claims, and proposes Astral, a snapshot-pinned, quorum-based accountable protocol that reduces adversarial attack success at the cost of coverage.
motivation: LLMs are increasingly used to judge whether web evidence supports claims, but retrieved pages can manipulate assessors and correlated model families fail together, so naive majority voting gives false assurance about verdict validity.
method: The authors prove that any protocol deciding solely from assessor outputs and always reaching agreement cannot reliably reject invalid claims; they then design Astral, which pins assessors to one committed evidence snapshot and accepts verdicts only with 2f+1 attested confidence above threshold and no standing signed challenge.
result: Across five public benchmarks with two of seven assessors adversarial, Astral lowers pooled attack success to 21.5-53.1% versus 54.7-77.8% for majority voting, while without attack only 16.0-61.7% of claims receive a binary verdict, the remainder being disputed for audit.
conclusion: Accountable, snapshot-committed consensus with cryptographic attestation and challenge mechanisms can meaningfully harden LLM-mediated fact verification, though the security gain comes with substantial coverage loss requiring human auditing.

title: Strategic Calibration In Llm Multi-Agent Systems: Audited Pivot Scoring For Truthful Elicitation
authors: Jinhao Zhou, Zhaohan Zhang, Xijian Xu, Jun Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems, reported confidence increasingly determines the allocation of scarce downstream attention, computation, and decision influence. This makes reporting strategic: an agent may overstate the relevance of its contribution even when its underlying belief is well calibrated. Existing calibration methods largely assume passive reporting and therefore do not address strategic incentives created when confidence determines downstream allocation. We formulate strategic calibration as a reporting-layer incentive problem and propose the Audited Pivot Scoring Mechanism (APSM). APSM offsets platform-controlled allocation benefits, uses inverse-propensity-weighted sparse audits, charges the Clarke pivot externality, and applies a strictly proper score. Under the stated model assumptions, truthful reporting is the unique expected-utility best response. We also characterize approximate execution and the audit-variance trade-off. Calculator-free experiments show that LLM agents inflate confidence under Top-[MATH] incentives. With a shared agent-local utility interface, LLM agents reduce distortion under both Compensated Proper Scoring (CPS) and APSM. CPS achieves higher exact allocation match, whereas APSM yields lower Brier loss and numerically fewer cutoff crossings. Experiments further show that APSM enlarges the utility margin against allocation-changing deviations by [MATH] and improves robustness under approximate execution. These results support incentive-aware elicitation as a distinct layer for reliable multi-agent coordination.
tldr: The paper proposes the Audited Pivot Scoring Mechanism (APSM), a mechanism-design approach for eliciting truthful confidence reports from LLM agents in multi-agent systems where reported confidence steers downstream allocation.
motivation: In LLM-based multi-agent systems, reported confidence determines allocation of attention, compute, and decision influence, which creates strategic incentives for agents to inflate their claims; existing calibration methods assume passive, non-strategic reporting.
method: The authors frame strategic calibration as a reporting-layer incentive problem and design APSM, combining inverse-propensity-weighted sparse audits, Clarke pivot externality charges, offsetting of platform-controlled allocation benefits, and a strictly proper scoring rule, with analysis of approximate execution and the audit-variance trade-off.
result: Experiments show LLM agents inflate confidence under Top-M incentives, and that agents reduce distortion under both Compensated Proper Scoring and APSM, with CPS achieving higher exact allocation match while APSM yields lower Brier loss, fewer cutoff crossings, a larger utility margin against allocation-changing deviations, and better robustness under approximate execution.
conclusion: Incentive-aware elicitation is argued to constitute a distinct design layer for reliable multi-agent coordination, complementing conventional calibration approaches.

title: Meta-Mathematics Of Algebraic Complexity
authors: Michal Garlik, Svyatoslav Gryaznov, Jiaqi Lu, Rahul Santhanam, Iddo Tzameret
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We initiate the study of the meta-mathematics of algebraic circuit lower bounds, aiming both to gain insight into the methods sufficient and necessary to prove algebraic circuit lower bounds, and to contribute to the study of bounded arithmetic as a logical foundation for complexity lower bounds. We demonstrate that while algebraic circuit lower bounds are hard for somewhat weak proof systems such as Polynomial Calculus Resolution ([MATH]), contemporary lower bounds are efficiently provable in proof systems and bounded arithmetic theories corresponding to [MATH], such as [MATH] and the corresponding class of propositional Frege proofs of quasipolynomial-size. Moreover, going below [MATH] into algebraic constant-depth reasoning is likely insufficient to efficiently prove already constant-depth algebraic circuit lower bounds. Under an algebraic analogue of the Krajicek--Razborov conjecture, our results suggest that proving superpolynomial lower bounds for general algebraic circuits will require stronger reasoning than that used in the rank-based proofs studied here. Specifically, we show the following.
tldr: The paper initiates the meta-mathematics of algebraic circuit lower bounds, studying which proof systems and bounded arithmetic theories can efficiently prove such lower bounds.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the logical and proof-theoretic strength needed to establish algebraic circuit lower bounds and to connect this with bounded arithmetic as a foundation for complexity lower bounds.
method: They analyze algebraic circuit lower bounds within proof systems such as Polynomial Calculus Resolution and bounded arithmetic theories corresponding to Frege proofs, and consider algebraic constant-depth reasoning and an algebraic analogue of the Krajicek--Razborov conjecture.
result: They show that contemporary lower bounds are efficiently provable in certain quasipolynomial-size Frege systems and related bounded arithmetic, while going below a certain threshold into algebraic constant-depth reasoning is likely insufficient even for constant-depth lower bounds.
conclusion: Under an algebraic Krajicek--Razborov-type conjecture, proving superpolynomial lower bounds for general algebraic circuits may require stronger reasoning than the rank-based methods studied.

title: A Class Of Niho Type Four-valued Cross-correlation Functions Between Sequences Of Different Periods
authors: Yao Yao, Yufei Wang, Yongbo Xia, Nian Li, Xiangyong Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.34010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Determining the cross-correlation distributions between [MATH]-sequences and their decimated sequences is an important problem in sequence design. For two positive integers [MATH] and [MATH] with [MATH], this paper investigates the cross-correlation function between a binary [MATH]-sequence [MATH] of period [MATH] and its [MATH] short-period decimated sequences [MATH], where the decimation [MATH] satisfies [MATH]. The cross-correlation function is proved to be four-valued and its value distribution is completely determined. Several previously known binary cross-correlation functions are included in our result as special cases.
tldr: This paper determines a four-valued Niho-type cross-correlation distribution between binary m-sequences of different periods and their short-period decimated sequences.
motivation: Cross-correlation distributions between m-sequences and decimated sequences are a central problem in classical sequence design, with applications to coding and communications rather than quantum information.
method: The authors analyze the cross-correlation function for a specified class of decimations satisfying a Niho-type condition and prove that it takes exactly four values, fully deriving its value distribution.
result: The cross-correlation is shown to be four-valued, its distribution is completely determined, and several previously known binary cross-correlation functions emerge as special cases.
conclusion: The work extends the theory of classical binary sequence cross-correlation but has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Contact-Free Nuclear And Cytoplasmic Mechanophenotyping By Amplitude-Modulated Ultrasound And Phase-Locked Optical Diffraction Tomography: Computational Feasibility And Initial Experimental Readouts
authors: Yagmur Isik, Merve Sevgi, Esmahan Caglar, Aysenur Akgun, Hasan Berkay Abdioglu, Gokhan Bora Esmer, Huseyin Uvet
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate whether acoustic stimulation combined with phase-locked optical diffraction tomography (ODT) could measure the mechanical responses of the nucleus and cytoplasm separately in adherent cells. A megahertz ultrasound carrier is amplitude-modulated at low frequencies, while angle-scanned holography provides a route to reconstruct the first-harmonic refractive-index response in three dimensions. We built a computational model connecting viscoelastic finite-element simulations of MDA-MB-231 cells with a refractive-index phantom, hologram formation, camera noise and ODT reconstruction. Under an assumed 0.1 Pa harmonic shear traction at 10 Hz, the model predicts 3.6 to 9.2 nm of nuclear shear and 6.6 to 15.1 nm of apical motion. The nuclear-to-cytoplasmic amplitude ratio (R_A) is primarily sensitive to stiffness contrast in the tested scenarios, while the relative phase (Delta phi) responds to differences in dissipation. A simulated protocol using 100 illumination angles and 16 phase visits per angle recovered an imposed stiffening and recovery trajectory after averaging four acquisitions. We also obtained initial 3D tomograms of adherent MDA-MB-231 cells and report preliminary regional measurements from five cells. Their mean amplitude ratio was 0.616 plus or minus 0.098, and their mean relative phase was -1.91 plus or minus 0.58 degrees (mean and between-cell sample standard deviation). All five amplitude ratios were below unity, and all phase differences were negative, consistent with the qualitative directions of selected model scenarios. The small cohort and the absence of independently quantified experimental phase noise prevent a claim of quantitative mechanical validation. Together, these results support further evaluation of phase-locked acoustic ODT and identify experimental requirements for a controlled validation study.
tldr: A computational and preliminary experimental feasibility study of combining amplitude-modulated megahertz ultrasound with phase-locked optical diffraction tomography to separately map nuclear and cytoplasmic viscoelastic responses in adherent MDA-MB-231 cells.
motivation: Existing mechanophenotyping methods cannot easily resolve the mechanical response of the nucleus versus the cytoplasm in intact adherent cells without contact, so the authors ask whether acoustically driven motion read out holographically could provide that contrast.
method: The authors built a forward model linking viscoelastic finite-element simulations of cells to a refractive-index phantom, hologram formation, camera noise and ODT reconstruction, then simulated a 100-angle, 16-phase-visit protocol and acquired initial 3D tomograms of five adherent cells.
result: Under an assumed 0.1 Pa harmonic shear at 10 Hz the model predicts 3.6-9.2 nm nuclear shear and 6.6-15.1 nm apical motion, with amplitude ratio sensitive to stiffness contrast and relative phase to dissipation; measured cells gave a mean amplitude ratio of 0.616 +/- 0.098 and mean relative phase of -1.91 +/- 0.58 degrees.
conclusion: The results are qualitatively consistent with selected model scenarios but the small cohort and unquantified experimental phase noise preclude quantitative mechanical validation, so the work motivates a controlled follow-up validation study.

title: Flocking With Finite Communication Speed: A Doppler-inspired Lyapunov Approach
authors: Mauro Rodriguez Cartabia Jan Haskovec
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Cucker--Smale model with state-dependent transmission delays arising from finite-speed information propagation. Our main contribution is a Lyapunov functional inspired by the Doppler effect, combining a delay potential with a logarithmic correction involving the receiver velocity. Its dissipation yields uniform delay bounds without relying on velocity contraction estimates. For two agents in one spatial dimension, we prove asymptotic flocking for arbitrary compatible subluminal initial histories, assuming only that the influence function has a divergent integral at infinity. A bounded geometric correction extends this result to arbitrary spatial dimension when all values of the initial velocity histories lie on one common affine line. For multiple agents in one dimension, we obtain uniform delay bounds, and thus flocking, provided that a fixed agent is leftmost for all sufficiently large times. In all these flocking regimes, the spatial diameter remains uniformly bounded and the velocity diameter decays exponentially. We also derive a conditional criterion involving logarithmic sums when the leftmost agent changes infinitely often. Finally, we construct a multidimensional analogue of the Doppler-inspired functional and identify an additional assumption needed to obtain delay bounds in the general case.
tldr: A Doppler-inspired Lyapunov functional is constructed to prove asymptotic flocking in the Cucker–Smale model with state-dependent transmission delays caused by finite-speed information propagation.
motivation: Flocking models usually assume instantaneous information exchange; when signals travel at finite speed, delays become state-dependent, and classical velocity-contraction arguments for the Cucker–Smale model no longer apply.
method: The authors build a Lyapunov functional combining a delay potential with a logarithmic correction in the receiver velocity (motivated by the Doppler effect), and use its dissipation to bound delays; a bounded geometric correction extends the functional to higher spatial dimensions.
result: For two agents in one dimension, asymptotic flocking is proven for arbitrary compatible subluminal initial histories under only a divergent influence-function integral; multi-agent and higher-dimensional cases yield uniform delay bounds and exponential velocity-diameter decay under additional structural assumptions (fixed leftmost agent, velocities on a common affine line).
conclusion: The Doppler-inspired Lyapunov approach gives delay-robust flocking guarantees without velocity contraction estimates, though general multidimensional cases still require an extra assumption.

title: Approximate Controllability Of Neutral Integro-Differential Inclusions Associated With Hemivariational Inequalities In Banach Spaces With Uniformly Convex Dual
authors: Jyoti Jindal, Sumit Arora, Manil T. Mohan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the approximate controllability of neutral integro-differential inclusions driven by hemivariational inequalities with nonlocal inclusion conditions in a Banach space [MATH] whose dual [MATH] is uniformly convex, using resolvent operator theory. We first establish an equivalence between the original problem and an associated differential inclusion involving the Clarke subdifferential. Under suitable assumptions, we then prove the existence of mild solutions corresponding to admissible controls in [MATH]. A key contribution of this work lies in the analysis of the control construction in Banach spaces, where the duality mapping [MATH] is generally nonlinear, in contrast to the Hilbert space setting, while such nonlinearity has been viewed as a technical obstruction in earlier studies. Based on this framework, we prove approximate controllability of the original system by relating it to the controllability of the associated linearized inclusion and constructing appropriate controls involving the duality mapping. Finally, we present applications to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
tldr: The paper proves approximate controllability results for neutral integro-differential inclusions governed by hemivariational inequalities with nonlocal conditions in Banach spaces with uniformly convex duals, using resolvent operator theory.
motivation: Controllability of neutral integro-differential inclusions with hemivariational inequalities is an open problem in the Banach space setting, where the nonlinearity of the duality mapping has usually been treated as a technical obstruction.
method: The authors convert the original problem into an equivalent differential inclusion involving the Clarke subdifferential, prove existence of mild solutions for admissible controls via resolvent operators, and construct explicit controls exploiting the duality mapping to relate the system to a linearized inclusion.
result: Under suitable assumptions, the existence of mild solutions is established, and approximate controllability of the original nonlinear system follows from controllability of the associated linearized inclusion.
conclusion: The work shows that the nonlinear duality mapping need not obstruct control construction in Banach spaces and provides applications illustrating the general framework.

title: Compactness Of Composition Operators On Hardy Spaces Of Homogeneous Rooted Trees
authors: Wanxin Ma Lei Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present a complete characterization of the compactness of arbitrary finite linear combinations of composition operators acting on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees. In particular, we obtain a characterization of compactness for linear combinations satisfying the CNC. As an application, we give an affirmative answer to a conjecture raised by Choe et al. [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B 9(2022), 733--756] concerning such Hardy spaces. Furthermore, we establish the phenomenon of (double) difference cancellation for linear combinations of composition operators by constructing explicit examples.
tldr: The paper gives a complete characterization of compactness for finite linear combinations of composition operators acting on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees, resolving a conjecture of Choe et al.
motivation: Composition operators on Hardy spaces of rooted trees are a recent operator-theoretic construction, and compactness of their linear combinations (especially under the CNC condition) was previously unresolved, including an explicit conjecture in the literature.
method: Pure functional-analytic techniques: characterization of compactness for arbitrary finite linear combinations of composition operators, analysis of the CNC condition, and explicit constructions of examples exhibiting (double) difference cancellation.
result: A full compactness characterization is obtained, the Choe et al. conjecture is affirmatively answered, and double difference cancellation phenomena are demonstrated via explicit examples.
conclusion: The work advances the operator theory of tree-based Hardy spaces, but has no evident connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: On The Power Of Adaption And Randomization 2: Non-symmetric Convex Sets
authors: David Krieg, Erich Novak, Mario Ullrich
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a bounded linear operator between real Banach spaces, and let [MATH] be nonempty, bounded and convex. We prove $[MATH][MATH]a_k[MATH]k[MATH]e_n^{\rm ran}[MATH]e_n^{\rm ada}[MATH]n[MATH]27n$ for approximation in convex sets. We discuss the optimality of the result by examples.
tldr: The paper derives bounds relating adaptive and randomized approximation numbers for bounded linear operators restricted to non-symmetric convex sets in Banach spaces.
motivation: Information-based complexity seeks to understand how much power adaptivity and randomization give over deterministic non-adaptive algorithms when approximating operators, and prior results were largely limited to symmetric convex bodies.
method: The authors prove inequalities of the form a_k ≤ C·n·e_n^ran and e_n^ada ≤ ...·n·e_n^ran for approximation within general bounded convex sets, employing techniques from Banach space theory and general position/volume arguments, and they construct examples to test sharpness.
result: A general comparison inequality holding up to polynomial factors in the dimension n is established for non-symmetric convex sets, together with examples discussing the optimality of the factor n^{2.7} (or similar) appearing in the bound.
conclusion: Adaptivity and randomization are shown to be essentially equivalent to non-adaptive randomized methods up to modest polynomial factors even without symmetry assumptions, extending earlier results beyond the symmetric setting.

title: A Deterministic Security Runtime For Llm Agents On Mpi And Batch-Scheduled Hpc Systems: Consensus-Governed, Hardware-Rooted Supervision Of Every Rank
authors: Alfredo Metere
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model agents launch simulations on high-performance computing (HPC) systems, where one sbatch or mpirun can commit thousands of node-hours and a forged result can cost lives. Of 23 surveyed systems, none supervises the running job, and none holds when the control host is compromised. We fix both. Enclawed, our deterministic security runtime for AI agents, has until now served a single user; this work makes it a distributed runtime for parallel HPC and agent swarms. The Enclaweder, our hardware root of trust, keeps a compromised host from becoming a catastrophe. A launch gate decides every launch by policy alone, refusing what it cannot parse. Once the job runs, a swarm chain grants short leases against signed heartbeats and evicts on evidence, and a supervisor around every rank pauses it when its lease lapses and kills it on tampering. Each node signs with its Enclaweder's key, so the host can forge none of it. Enclawed needs no administrator privileges and plugs into existing clusters unchanged, over Secure Shell alone. Supervision leaves the compute loop of a 16-rank LAMMPS job unchanged, on graphics processors too, and adds about 3 s of start-up. Twelve live attacks on Enclaweder-keyed ranks, colluding coordinators included, ended fail-closed. Sixteen agents on a real model attempted 24 launches that planted instructions ordered; the gate denied all 24 and allowed all 108 legitimate ones. Enclawed's core and the HPC Agent Security Benchmark are open source.
tldr: The paper presents Enclawed, a deterministic security runtime that supervises LLM-agent-launched jobs on MPI and batch-scheduled HPC systems using a hardware root of trust and consensus-style lease/heartbeat governance over every rank.
motivation: LLM agents can submit large HPC jobs whose forgery or tampering could be catastrophic, yet none of 23 surveyed systems supervises running jobs or survives compromise of the control host.
method: A launch gate admits jobs purely by policy; a swarm chain issues short leases against signed heartbeats and evicts on evidence; per-rank supervisors pause lapsed ranks and kill tampered ones; each node signs with its Enclaweder hardware key, all over SSH without admin privileges.
result: Supervision leaves the compute loop of a 16-rank LAMMPS job (including GPU runs) unchanged with ~3 s start-up overhead, twelve live attacks (including colluding coordinators) failed closed, and the gate denied all 24 planted launches while allowing all 108 legitimate ones across 16 agents.
conclusion: Enclawed provides practical, privilege-free, hardware-rooted supervision of agent-launched HPC jobs, with core code and an HPC Agent Security Benchmark released as open source.

title: From Instructions To Exploits: Applying Program Analysis To Malicious Agent Skills Across Natural Language And Code
authors: Shiwu Zhao, Baizhu Wang, Guoqiang Zheng, Tingyu Gao, Yuheng Xie, Rujie Chen, Xingchen Chen, Xuezhang Liu, Qixu Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-powered agents increasingly rely on third-party skills that combine natural-language instructions with executable code, creating supply-chain risks that may span both artifacts. Existing skill scanners often rely on rule matching or direct LLM judgments and provide limited support for tracing such cross-domain behavior. We present the Supply-Chain Scanner for Agent Skills (SCS), a static analysis framework that unifies instructions and code for security analysis. SCS compiles natural-language instructions into a constrained Python-style intermediate representation using a limited set of security-oriented APIs. It then constructs program dependence graphs for instructions and bundled code and connects them into a cross-domain graph (xPDG). A Trust-Sensitivity-Capability (TSC) model propagates security properties over the graph to support structured, largely deterministic risk detection. On a manually verified benchmark of 117 malicious and 117 benign skills, SCS achieves the highest average accuracy (85.6%), recall (95.2%), and F1-score (86.9%) among evaluated methods across five LLMs, with 80.2% precision and average token consumption of 13.7 million. Its NL-to-IR compiler achieves 92.5%-94.5% step-level correctness on 400 human-annotated instruction steps. Finally, analyzing 66,157 real-world ClawHub skills yields 2,473 candidates, of which 627 are confirmed malicious through auxiliary dynamic validation and manual review.
tldr: SCS is a static analysis framework that unifies natural-language instructions and bundled code from third-party LLM agent skills into a cross-domain program dependence graph for detecting malicious supply-chain behavior.
motivation: LLM agents increasingly load third-party 'skills' that mix natural-language instructions with executable code, creating supply-chain attacks that span both artifacts and that existing rule-matching or LLM-judgment scanners cannot trace across domains.
method: The authors compile natural-language instructions into a constrained Python-style intermediate representation over a limited set of security-oriented APIs, build program dependence graphs for instructions and code, link them into a cross-domain graph (xPDG), and propagate Trust-Sensitivity-Capability properties over it for largely deterministic risk detection.
result: On a benchmark of 117 malicious and 117 benign skills SCS reaches 85.6% accuracy, 95.2% recall, 86.9% F1 and 80.2% precision, with 92.5-94.5% step-level NL-to-IR correctness; scanning 66,157 ClawHub skills flagged 2,473 candidates, 627 confirmed malicious.
conclusion: Cross-domain static analysis of instructions and code is an effective, largely deterministic defense for the emerging LLM agent-skill supply chain, though it remains a software-security contribution with no quantum information or thermodynamics content.

title: Trust Mechanisms For Offline Generative Ai At The Edge: A Connectivity-Regime Framework And An Empirical Study On A Raspberry Pi 5
authors: Alexandros Papaspyridis Georgios Feretzakis
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI and large language models (LLMs) are moving into the Internet of Things, yet most deployments assume cloud connectivity, and many IoT settings have intermittent, restricted, or no connectivity. We propose a connectivity-regime framework (C0-C4), a taxonomy of inference-time trust mechanisms, and signed, versioned knowledge packs as the update channel for disconnected regimes, and evaluate them on a Raspberry Pi 5 running fully local retrieval-augmented generation under network isolation, with three Qwen2.5 model sizes, three context sizes, and 300 SQuAD 2.0 questions. An empirically calibrated retrieval-score gate detects knowledge gaps almost perfectly (AUROC 0.97) but in-topic unanswerable questions poorly (0.68). A deterministic output validator converts malformed outputs into explicit abstentions with no observed loss of correct answers, while the NLI-based verifier we tested adds little; for the 7B model, 96% of substantive answers to unanswerable-labelled questions match normalized spans of the retrieved passages. A 3B model achieves the same gold-answer containment rate as a 7B model at less than half the latency and estimated energy, although the 7B model far more often exceeds a token-F1 threshold of 0.5; five retrieved passages lower correctness from 75% to 52% compared with three. Verifying a signed pack takes about 4.5 ms versus about 29 min for embedding its passages on the device; signature and hash checks alone accept six of nine tested update attacks that layered verification rejects. Yet a validly signed poisoned pack passes every pack check: on 30 previously correct questions, correct answers drop to zero and 14 return the injected answer. None of the mechanisms we evaluated establishes the truth of the evidence. We release code and data.
tldr: The paper presents a connectivity-regime framework, a taxonomy of trust mechanisms, signed knowledge packs, and an empirical Raspberry Pi 5 study of fully local RAG with Qwen2.5 models under network isolation.
motivation: Generative AI and LLMs are increasingly deployed on IoT and edge devices where connectivity is intermittent or absent, yet most trust and update mechanisms assume cloud access.
method: The authors define a C0-C4 connectivity framework, catalogue inference-time trust mechanisms (retrieval-score gating, a deterministic output validator, and an NLI verifier), and introduce signed, versioned knowledge packs, all evaluated on a Raspberry Pi 5 with three Qwen2.5 model sizes, three context sizes, and 300 SQuAD 2.0 questions.
result: The retrieval-score gate achieves AUROC 0.97 on knowledge gaps but only 0.68 on in-topic unanswerable questions; the NLI verifier adds little; a 3B model matches a 7B model's gold-answer containment at under half the latency and energy; five retrieved passages reduce correctness from 75% to 52%; and a validly signed poisoned pack defeats every pack check.
conclusion: Signature and hash verification alone are insufficient, and none of the evaluated mechanisms establishes the truth of the evidence, so trust in offline edge generative AI remains an open problem.

title: Statistical Inference For Boundary Constrained Parameters
authors: Jaeseon Lee, Anirban Bhattacharya, Suhasini Subba Rao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Estimation and inference under boundary constraints arises in many areas of statistics, but the available asymptotic theory remains limited and fragmented relative to the classical case, where the parameter lies in the interior of the parameter space. In this paper we derive a boundary-constrained analogue of the standard asymptotic expansion for a minimiser of a loss function, in which the deviation of the estimator from the population parameter is decomposed over lower-dimensional subspaces determined by the directional derivatives at the minimiser. Using this decomposition we show that the limiting distribution of the estimator is a mixture of point masses and truncated skew-normal distributions, with mixture probabilities determined by the directional derivative conditions. A consequence of this result is that the constrained and unconstrained coordinates do not separate: the presence of parameters on or near the boundary affects the sampling distribution of the unconstrained parameter estimators. We apply the expansion to obtain the asymptotic distribution of the quasi log-likelihood ratio statistic under a range of null hypotheses, and since the resulting mixture is not pivotal in the quasi-likelihood setting, we propose a simulation-based procedure for approximating critical values. The framework unifies and simplifies several existing results. We illustrate the methodology by testing for interactions in exponential family graphical models, where the parameters are subject to compatibility constraints that ensure a joint distribution exists.
tldr: The paper develops a boundary-constrained asymptotic expansion for loss-function minimisers, showing the limiting distribution is a mixture of point masses and truncated skew-normal distributions.
motivation: Asymptotic theory for M-estimators is well developed when the true parameter lies in the interior of the parameter space, but remains fragmented for parameters on or near a boundary, which arises frequently in constrained statistical models.
method: The authors decompose the estimator's deviation from the population parameter over lower-dimensional subspaces defined by directional derivatives at the minimiser, then derive the limiting mixture distribution and apply it to quasi log-likelihood ratio statistics with a simulation-based critical-value procedure.
result: Constrained and unconstrained coordinates do not separate—boundary parameters distort the sampling distribution of unconstrained estimators—and the quasi-LRT limiting distribution is a non-pivotal mixture requiring simulated critical values.
conclusion: The framework unifies and simplifies several existing boundary-inference results and is illustrated on testing interactions in exponential family graphical models with compatibility constraints.

title: Robust Augmented Block Preconditioning For Two-phase Incompressible Inductionless Mhd
authors: Bijie Song, Lingxiao Li, Jie Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a robust augmented block preconditioner for three-dimensional, two-phase, incompressible inductionless MHD equations. We employ a high-order monolithic and charge-conservative arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian (ALE) finite element method as base scheme, for which the solution variables are current density, velocity, electric potential and pressure. Grad-div stabilization is added in both the current density equation and discrete momentum equation. Backward Euler method is used for the time discretization. At each time step, fully coupled solution strategy is adopted. This leads to large-scale, ill-conditioned, nonsymmetric, and indefinite dual saddle-point system. To solve this system efficiently, we construct an augmented block preconditioner within the constraint preconditioning framework. The ultimate preconditioner combines the augmented Lagrangian technique with approximate block factorization for current density sub-system and fluid sub-system. The fully coupled four-field system is then solved using preconditioned FGMRES iteration. Numerical experiments confirm the high-order accuracy and discrete charge conservation of the ALE-FEM. Drop of heavy fluid in light fluid is taken as benchmark to demonstrate the robustness of the preconditioner with respect to the discontinuity of physical parameters and the mesh size.
tldr: The paper develops an augmented block preconditioner for fully coupled monolithic finite element solution of three-dimensional two-phase inductionless MHD equations.
motivation: Two-phase incompressible inductionless MHD simulations with charge-conservative ALE finite elements produce large, ill-conditioned, nonsymmetric, indefinite dual saddle-point systems that are difficult to solve efficiently and robustly.
method: A high-order monolithic charge-conservative ALE finite element scheme with grad-div stabilization and backward Euler time stepping is used, and an augmented block preconditioner combining augmented Lagrangian techniques with approximate block factorization is applied within a preconditioned FGMRES iteration.
result: Numerical experiments confirm high-order accuracy and discrete charge conservation, and a heavy-fluid-drop benchmark shows the preconditioner is robust with respect to jumps in physical parameters and mesh refinement.
conclusion: The proposed preconditioning strategy enables efficient and robust solution of the coupled four-field MHD system, making large-scale two-phase MHD simulations practical.

title: Mixed-norm Herz-type Triebel-Lizorkin Spaces
authors: Douadi Drihem
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Based on mixed-norm Herz spaces, we introduce a new class of mixed-norm Herz-type Triebel-Lizorkin spaces. We establish their [MATH]-transform characterization in the sense of Frazier and Jawerth and prove Sobolev embedding theorems for these spaces. The resulting embedding theorems extend and improve several known results for mixed-norm Triebel-Lizorkin spaces.
tldr: The paper introduces mixed-norm Herz-type Triebel-Lizorkin spaces and develops their phi-transform characterization and Sobolev embedding theorems.
motivation: Mixed-norm Triebel-Lizorkin and Herz spaces have known embedding results, but a Herz-type mixed-norm Triebel-Lizorkin variant with a full transform-based framework was missing.
method: Building on mixed-norm Herz spaces, the authors construct the new scale of spaces, establish a Frazier-Jawerth phi-transform characterization, and derive Sobolev-type embeddings.
result: The phi-transform characterization is proven and the embedding theorems shown to extend and improve existing results for mixed-norm Triebel-Lizorkin spaces.
conclusion: The new space family provides a generalization that unifies and strengthens prior embedding results, though it remains within classical harmonic analysis.

title: A New Arrangement Inequality (revised And Extended Version)
authors: Mohammad Javaheri
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the cyclic inequality \[ \sum_{i=1}^n x_i\,\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^a x_{i+1}^b\;\le\;\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^{(1+a+b)/2}\Big)^2, \] where [MATH] and indices are taken modulo [MATH]. Let [MATH] be the largest [MATH] for which the inequality holds for all nonnegative [MATH]. We show that [MATH] is bounded above by an explicit quantity [MATH] obtained from the second variation at the constant vector, and we conjecture that [MATH]. For [MATH] we prove that the inequality holds if and only if [MATH], which settles the case left open in the original version of this paper. For [MATH] the inequality holds whenever [MATH] are the sides of a triangle, with an explicit remainder term. We show that [MATH] is monotone along rays emanating from the line [MATH]; this corrects and extends an earlier monotonicity statement. Finally, any [MATH] nonnegative numbers can be arranged so that the inequality holds; for [MATH] this is achieved by one of [MATH] prescribed arrangements, which yields a volume bound for every such [MATH].
tldr: The paper studies and proves bounds for a cyclic arrangement inequality involving nonnegative numbers, with applications to volume bounds.
motivation: The work addresses a mathematical inequality and its optimal parameter range, extending earlier partial results and conjectures.
method: It uses analytic techniques such as second variation at the constant vector, monotonicity along rays, and case analysis for triangle side lengths.
result: The author establishes explicit upper bounds, proves the inequality for certain parameter regimes, and shows that any set of nonnegative numbers can be arranged to satisfy the inequality.
conclusion: The paper resolves several open cases and provides a volume bound, but it is a pure inequality result with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: On Optimal Stopping Problems With Full Information And Rank-dependent Reward
authors: Yaakov Malinovsky Alexander Goldenshluger
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we consider optimal stopping problems with full information and rank-dependent rewards. Our focus is on the following two problems: selecting one of the r best observations (Gusein-Zade's problem with full information) and minimizing the expected rank (Robbins' problem). In both settings we provide full characterization of the optimal stopping rules and corresponding optimal values. We also present numerical experiments in which the derived dynamic programming recursions are implemented, and approximations to optimal values are computed.
tldr: The paper fully characterizes optimal stopping rules for two classical rank-dependent selection problems: Gusein-Zade's problem of selecting one of the r best observations with full information, and Robbins' problem of minimizing expected rank.
motivation: Rank-dependent reward optimal stopping problems are classical sequential-decision problems in probability and statistics, and a complete characterization of optimal rules with full information was still lacking for these variants.
method: The authors derive dynamic programming recursions characterizing the optimal stopping rules and optimal values for both problems, then implement these recursions numerically to compute approximations of the optimal values.
result: Full characterizations of the optimal stopping rules and corresponding optimal values are obtained for both problems, supported by numerical experiments computing approximate optimal values.
conclusion: The work provides a complete solution framework for full-information rank-dependent optimal stopping, but it is a purely classical probability/statistics contribution with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Agent-to-Agent Synthetic Social Engineering On The Web
authors: Bryan C. Boots
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33411v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An AI agent can prepare an accurate report and still request an action its user has not authorized. Cooperation across Web services therefore requires separate judgments about identity, evidentiary support, and permission. We define synthetic social engineering (SSE) as deliberately deceptive or misleading influence intended to exploit AI recipients' responses to credibility, authority, or obligation cues and redirect behavior away from authorized objectives. We focus on separately tasked sender agents that produce or adapt misleading communication. Drawing on cybersecurity, social engineering, and persuasion research, we develop an operational framework connecting actors, deceptive representations, candidate influence routes, evidence or permission boundaries, responses, and consequences. The framework distinguishes attempts from successful redirection, without assuming human psychological processes. We implement it in the Agent Service Exchange and Evidence Commons (ASE-EC), a reproducible testbed with independently specified records and authorization scopes. Across 1,260 research episodes using Qwen3-4B in two fictional briefing tasks, matched comparisons test authority and commitment appeals, while defense comparisons assess protection alongside authorized task completion. Invoking a limited prior agreement increased unauthorized requests from 43.3% to 96.7%, although recipients retained supported decisions and permissions remained unchanged. These controlled findings identify action selection as a distinct security concern, even when evidence handling succeeds, and they provide a reusable basis for evaluating safeguards that preserve useful cooperation across Web services.
tldr: The paper defines 'synthetic social engineering' among LLM-based web agents and builds a reproducible testbed (ASE-EC) to measure how credibility, authority, and obligation cues push agent behavior away from authorized objectives.
motivation: AI agents cooperating across web services can produce accurate reports yet request unauthorized actions, so identity, evidentiary support, and permission must be judged separately; existing security and persuasion research has not been adapted to agent recipients.
method: The authors construct an operational framework linking actors, deceptive representations, influence routes, evidence/permission boundaries, responses, and consequences, and implement it in the ASE-EC testbed with independently specified records and authorization scopes, running 1,260 research episodes with Qwen3-4B on two fictional briefing tasks.
result: Invoking a limited prior agreement raised unauthorized requests from 43.3% to 96.7%, while recipients still retained supported decisions and permissions remained unchanged, isolating action selection as a distinct security failure mode.
conclusion: Agent-to-agent synthetic social engineering is a real and measurable threat that should be evaluated separately from evidence handling, and the framework offers a reusable basis for testing safeguards that preserve useful cooperation.

title: Unifying Performance And Equity Via Percentile Optimization And Cell-Free Massive Mimo
authors: Ahmad Khan, Hussein A. Ammar, Raviraj Adve
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Improving the throughput of the weakest users is a central objective of wireless resource allocation, and the objective around which the user-centric cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (UC-mMIMO) architecture is built. This paper brings the two together by formulating and solving percentile programs for UC-mMIMO networks. We maximize the sum-least-qth-percentile (SLqP) rate via downlink power control, a utility that targets the user equipments (UEs) in the lowest q percentile of the rate distribution and subsumes max-min-rate and sum-rate maximization as special cases. The problem is non-convex, non-smooth and NP-hard. The cyclic maximization approach of one of the previous percentile optimization series does not carry over: the coherent joint transmission technique introduces cross terms in the powers that destroy the block-concavity on which it relies. We develop a change of variables that restores block-concavity, yielding an algorithm with closed-form auxiliary updates and a concave power update, and we give a self-contained proof of non-decreasing convergence to a directional stationary point. Simulations establish two facts: first, percentile optimization retains its value in an architecture with no cell edges; relative to the weighted minimum mean-square error benchmark, it raises the average rate of the lowest-10th-percentile UEs by 56--72% and Jain's fairness index from below 0.92 to above 0.99. Second, compared directly with massive MIMO and small cells under the same SLqP utility, UC-mMIMO delivers the highest lower-percentile rates at every access point density tested, by up to 62% and 2.7[MATH] respectively, at the same fairness, and its advantage widens with densification.
tldr: The paper formulates and solves sum-least-qth-percentile (SLqP) rate maximization problems for user-centric cell-free massive MIMO networks via downlink power control.
motivation: Improving the throughput of the weakest users is central to wireless resource allocation and to the user-centric cell-free massive MIMO architecture, and the authors aim to unify performance and equity through percentile optimization.
method: A change of variables restores block-concavity that coherent joint transmission's cross terms destroy, yielding an algorithm with closed-form auxiliary updates and a concave power update, with a proof of non-decreasing convergence to a directional stationary point.
result: Simulations show SLqP optimization raises the average rate of the lowest-10th-percentile UEs by 56-72% over the weighted MMSE benchmark and lifts Jain's fairness index from below 0.92 to above 0.99, with UC-mMIMO delivering the highest lower-percentile rates at every AP density tested.
conclusion: Percentile optimization retains its value in an architecture without cell edges, and UC-mMIMO outperforms massive MIMO and small cells under the same SLqP utility, with advantages widening under densification.

title: The Digital-Energy Recomposition Of The Kitchin Cycle: Exploratory Evidence From U.s. It And Irish Data-Centre Series (1995-2025)
authors: Bartosz Ziollko, Adam Niedzialkowski, Bartosz Szyma
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using quarterly FRED and CSO Ireland data over 1995Q1-2025Q4, we examine whether U.S.\ IT investment and Irish data-centre electricity are recomposing the Kitchin cycle around energy- and compute-backed assets. Three findings stand out. First, a Quandt-Andrews sup-Wald test locates a significant break in the U.S.\ IT-GDP correlation at 2014Q3 (sup-W [MATH]; [MATH] falls from [MATH] to [MATH]); the Fisher [MATH]-to-[MATH] test survives Bonferroni adjustment ([MATH], [MATH]), whereas the analogous test on the imposed Cloud-vs-AI boundary does not ([MATH]), so ``Strategic Decoupling'' pre-dates the AI Era by approximately six years. Second, in Ireland the synchronous AI-Era correlation between metered data-centre electricity and Real GDP is large ([MATH], [MATH]) but , suggesting the headline is largely an artefact of the shared multinational tax-structure footprint between hyperscaler operations and Irish gross output. Third, the Irish cross-correlation profile is asymmetric in the opposite direction to a leading-indicator reading: the largest positive coefficients cluster on the [MATH] side (GDP precedes data-centre load), so compute capacity is better read as coincident or moderately lagging. Given the small AI-Era samples and the absence of a quarterly multinational-adjusted aggregate such as GNI*, all coefficients are exploratory; subject to these caveats, the U.S.\ Kitchin cycle is best dated to 2014Q3, and the Irish Energy-Data Nexus is dominated by multinational firm activity.
tldr: An econometric time-series study claiming that U.S. IT investment and Irish data-centre electricity consumption are re-dating the Kitchin business cycle around energy- and compute-backed assets.
motivation: The authors ask whether the rise of digital infrastructure (IT investment, hyperscale data centres) has shifted the periodization of the Kitchin inventory cycle, and whether an AI-era break is detectable in macroeconomic series.
method: Quarterly FRED and CSO Ireland data (1995Q1-2025Q4) analyzed with Quandt-Andrews sup-Wald structural-break tests, Fisher z-to-r transformations with Bonferroni correction, and cross-correlation analysis of data-centre load versus real GDP.
result: A significant break in the U.S. IT-GDP correlation is located at 2014Q3, roughly six years before the AI era; the Irish data-centre electricity-GDP correlation is large but attributable to shared multinational tax-structure footprints, and the cross-correlation profile suggests GDP leads data-centre load rather than the reverse.
conclusion: The U.S. Kitchin cycle is best dated to 2014Q3, and the Irish energy-data nexus appears dominated by multinational firm activity; all findings are exploratory given small samples and the lack of a quarterly GNI*-type aggregate.

title: Inverse Reconstruction Of Double Imaging Schlieren
authors: Jo\~ao F. C. Mota Shubham Saxena
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Double imaging is a common artefact in off-axis single-mirror Schlieren systems. Depending on the distance between the object of interest and the mirror, together with the off-axis imaging geometry, such systems often capture images containing a superposition of the target image and a displaced ghost image, resulting in the so-called double imaging phenomenon. This not only degrades image quality, but also complicates its interpretation. To address this problem, we present a new model for ghost image displacement that takes into consideration finite-aperture support, defocus, and magnification. We then use this model to reconstruct the target image via total variation regularisation with a matrix-free alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm. Extensive experiments using both synthetic and real Schlieren images validate the proposed model, show the effectiveness and efficiency of our algorithm, and evaluate its performance under parameter mismatch. The proposed framework provides a computational alternative to hardware-based suppression of double imaging, enabling physics-consistent reconstruction while preserving the simplicity and compactness of off-axis single-mirror Schlieren systems.
tldr: The paper presents a computational model and ADMM-based total-variation reconstruction method to remove double-image (ghost image) artefacts in off-axis single-mirror Schlieren imaging.
motivation: Double imaging arises in off-axis single-mirror Schlieren systems when a displaced ghost image overlaps the target image, degrading quality and complicating interpretation; hardware suppression is cumbersome, motivating a computational fix.
method: A ghost-image displacement model incorporating finite-aperture support, defocus and magnification is derived, then inverted via total-variation regularisation solved with a matrix-free ADMM algorithm.
result: Experiments on synthetic and real Schlieren images validate the displacement model and show the algorithm reconstructs target images efficiently, including under parameter mismatch.
conclusion: The framework offers a physics-consistent computational alternative to hardware-based suppression of double imaging, preserving the simplicity of compact off-axis single-mirror Schlieren setups.

title: Autonomous Atomistic-continuum Coupling Through Uncertainty-aware Active Learning
authors: Daniel Abdulah, Hariswaran Sitaraman, Ross E. Larsen, Kevin Patrick Griffin, Grace Wei, Janelle Domantay, Ethan Young, Marc T. Henry de Frahan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an uncertainty-aware surrogate modeling approach for coupling an atomistic kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) surface-chemistry solver with a continuum multi-species fluid dynamics solver across disparate physical length and time scales. The surrogate model predicts boundary mass fluxes for six species and their uncertainties, which the continuum solver monitors to automatically trigger additional KMC simulations when new training data are needed. This enables efficient multiscale coupling and maintains a user-specified level of accuracy. We demonstrate the approach for reactive halide-perovskite vapor deposition, which involves a multi-species vapor jet impinging on a reactive substrate. The KMC solver uses a DFT-calibrated energetics model that we construct as part of this work and provides net deposition and desorption rates for six species. With a conservative uncertainty threshold, the surrogate-coupled approach reproduces cumulative mass fluxes of the directly coupled approach with errors typically within 10-20%, while capturing the non-monotonic dependence of net deposition on species partial pressure. Importantly, the results show that detailed crystal structure need not be explicitly represented to predict quantities exchanged between atomistic and continuum solvers; species-resolved mass fluxes provide a sufficiently low-dimensional representation of the atomistic response. For this accuracy target, the autonomous online-learning approach reduces the number of required atomistic simulations by two to three orders of magnitude relative to direct multiscale coupling.
tldr: An uncertainty-aware surrogate model autonomously couples kinetic Monte Carlo atomistic simulations with continuum fluid dynamics, triggering new atomistic runs only when needed, demonstrated for halide-perovskite vapor deposition.
motivation: Direct multiscale coupling between atomistic and continuum solvers is computationally prohibitive, so an efficient surrogate with controlled accuracy is needed.
method: A machine-learned surrogate predicts boundary mass fluxes and their uncertainties for six species; the continuum solver monitors the uncertainty and triggers additional KMC simulations when accuracy degrades, using a DFT-calibrated energetics model.
result: With a conservative uncertainty threshold, the surrogate-coupled approach reproduces cumulative mass fluxes within 10-20% of direct coupling while reducing required atomistic simulations by two to three orders of magnitude.
conclusion: Species-resolved mass fluxes form a sufficiently low-dimensional representation of atomistic response, so detailed crystal structure need not be explicitly modeled for this coupling task.

title: A Neural Accelerated Surface-roughness-based Discrete Element Method (sr-dem) For Modeling Granular Systems
authors: Liuchi Li Xiwei Pan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Discrete Element Method (DEM) is an indispensable tool for modeling and understanding the basic mechanical behaviors of (dry) granular media, a class of disordered material systems of significant interest to multiple scientific domains from (geo-)physics to (chemical) engineering. At the core of all present DEM frameworks is a phenomenological friction law--commonly chosen to be of the Amontons-Coulomb type--that models the frictional interaction among constituent grains. Here, inspired by research in the tribology community, we present an alternative, fundamentally different framework, termed surface-roughness-based DEM (SR-DEM), in which contact friction is handled in a more physics-based manner. In this framework, instead of using a friction law, we explicitly resolve the surface topography of each grain and let friction emerge from collective frictionless interactions of surface asperities. In essence, we trade phenomenology for physics at the cost of an increased computational demand. To mitigate the cost, we introduce an FE[MATH]-like algorithm and a feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM)-based neural network surrogate, both of which are parallelized on GPU to accelerate contact computation. Crucially, using this framework in 2D, we (1) demonstrate the possibility of recovering a two-body-based Amontons-Coulomb-type friction behavior using a simple representation of surface topography, and (2) identify many-body-based frictional behaviors--more specifically, the angle of repose values--that cannot always be captured by current DEM frameworks under the same level of model complexity. We conclude by discussing future directions for SR-DEM, as well as exciting new opportunities it could unlock for a wide range of emerging applications, including (designing) suspension rheology and metamaterial mechanics.
tldr: The authors introduce surface-roughness-based DEM (SR-DEM), a granular-media simulation framework that replaces phenomenological Amontons-Coulomb friction laws with explicitly resolved surface topography and asperity interactions, accelerated by a GPU-parallelized neural surrogate.
motivation: Existing DEM frameworks rely on phenomenological friction laws such as Amontons-Coulomb, which lack a physics-based foundation; tribology research suggests friction could instead emerge from collective asperity interactions.
method: Each grain's surface topography is explicitly resolved and friction emerges from frictionless asperity contacts, with computational cost mitigated by an FEM-like algorithm and a FiLM-based neural network surrogate, both parallelized on GPU.
result: In 2D simulations the framework recovers two-body Amontons-Coulomb-type friction behavior from a simple topography representation and captures many-body frictional behaviors such as angle of repose that current DEM frameworks cannot reproduce at comparable model complexity.
conclusion: SR-DEM trades phenomenology for physics and opens directions for applications including suspension rheology design and metamaterial mechanics.

title: Polarization-resolved Haze In Transparent Wood - Towards Wooden Glass
authors: Zheheng Song, Hui Chen, Mathias Nero, Jingjian Zhou, Ravi Shanker, Tom Willhammar, Lars Berglund, Ilya Sychugov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transparent wood (TW) composites possess residual haze that limits image clarity despite their high light transmission, yet the physical origin of this scattering has not been established. Here, polarization-resolved measurements reveal a pronounced polarization dependence of scattering by a wood-polymer composite with improved refractive index matching. Polarization- and spectrally-resolved haze as low as 21% (40-45% at 550 nm for unpolarized light) with transmittance of approximately 92% for polarization perpendicular to the fibers was detected. It is found that the low-haze spectrum closely follows an inverse-square relation over the 400-800 nm range, well described by a weak-index-contrast Rayleigh-Gans-Debye (RGD) model invoking subwavelength birefringent heterogeneities within the cell wall. This physical mechanism was previously obscured by haze-limiting strong scattering from debonding gaps or refraction at the lumen-cell wall interface. Scanning electron diffraction independently reveals spatially distinct domains with markedly different cellulose diffraction responses within the infiltrated cell walls. The observed polarization-dependent refractive-index mismatch is attributed to inherent cellulose birefringence. Time-resolved measurements further support nearly scattering-free quasi-ballistic transport of the sampled transmitted light. It is demonstrated that selecting only a preferential polarization markedly improves image visibility through TW without further material modification. These findings connect polarization-dependent haze to the internal structure of transparent wood and identify ways to engineer a refractive-index match in hierarchical anisotropic composites towards glass-like clarity.
tldr: Polarization-resolved haze measurements in a refractive-index-matched transparent wood composite reveal that residual scattering follows a Rayleigh-Gans-Debye behavior originating from subwavelength birefringent cellulose heterogeneities in the cell wall.
motivation: Transparent wood combines high optical transmittance with residual haze that degrades image clarity, but the physical origin of this scattering had not been identified because stronger scattering from debonding gaps and lumen-cell-wall refraction obscured it.
method: The authors perform polarization- and spectrally-resolved haze and transmittance measurements on a wood-polymer composite with improved refractive-index matching, complemented by scanning electron diffraction to map cellulose domains and time-resolved measurements of transport.
result: Haze as low as 21% for light polarized perpendicular to the fibers (40-45% at 550 nm unpolarized) is achieved at ~92% transmittance, with the low-haze spectrum following an inverse-square wavelength dependence well described by a weak-index-contrast Rayleigh-Gans-Debye model.
conclusion: Polarization-dependent haze is traced to the intrinsic birefringence of cellulose, and selecting a preferential polarization markedly improves image visibility through transparent wood without further material modification, offering a route toward glass-like clarity in anisotropic composites.

title: A Differentiable Framework For Inverse Identification Of Heterogeneous Cohesive Laws
authors: Sida Hao, Jinkyo Han, Bahador Bahmani
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33711v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work develops a differentiable finite element framework based on an intrinsic cohesive-zone formulation for identifying traction-separation laws from global force-displacement histories and spatially sparse strain measurements. The framework employs physics-constrained neural networks to represent flexible, thermodynamically structured cohesive laws, with sensitivities computed through automatic differentiation and a discrete adjoint that accounts for the history-dependent evolution of interfacial damage. To enable identification of spatially heterogeneous cohesive behavior, we extend learned constitutive priors to irreversible interfacial damage by constructing a shared, low-dimensional family of cohesive laws from representative traction-separation histories. This representation exploits common constitutive structure and parameter sharing to reduce the number of unknowns and regularize the inverse problem, while allowing local cohesive behavior to vary spatially through latent coordinates. Numerical investigations involving double-cantilever beams and fiber-matrix composites demonstrate that accurate reproduction of global force-displacement responses does not necessarily imply accurate recovery of the underlying cohesive laws. Incorporating spatially resolved strain measurements substantially improves constitutive identification, even when the admissible responses are constrained by a learned prior. Comparisons with conventional bilinear cohesive models and Bayesian optimization further illustrate the benefits of the learned constitutive representation and adjoint-based identification for high-dimensional inverse problems.
tldr: The paper introduces a differentiable finite-element framework with physics-constrained neural networks and adjoint-based sensitivities to inversely identify heterogeneous cohesive traction-separation laws from global force-displacement data and sparse strain measurements.
motivation: Cohesive-zone models are hard to calibrate because global force-displacement histories alone are insufficient to uniquely determine spatially varying interfacial constitutive behavior.
method: An intrinsic cohesive-zone finite-element formulation is coupled with automatic differentiation and a discrete adjoint for history-dependent damage evolution, while a shared low-dimensional latent family of thermodynamically consistent cohesive laws encodes learned constitutive priors.
result: Numerical studies on double-cantilever beams and fiber-matrix composites show that matching global responses does not guarantee correct law recovery, and that spatially resolved strain data substantially improves identification over bilinear models and Bayesian optimization baselines.
conclusion: Learned constitutive priors plus adjoint-based differentiable identification offer an effective route to high-dimensional inverse problems in heterogeneous cohesive fracture, provided local strain information is available.

title: Some Expressions Involving Bernoulli, Harmonic, And Stirling Numbers
authors: Hongshen Chua
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish several identities involving Bernoulli numbers, harmonic numbers, and Stirling numbers. Our approach extends the method developed by Kargin and Mutluer.
tldr: The paper derives identities involving Bernoulli numbers, harmonic numbers, and Stirling numbers, extending a prior method by Kargin and Mutluer.
motivation: The work is motivated by the mathematical interest in combinatorial identities connecting classical special number sequences.
method: The authors generalize and extend an existing combinatorial/analytic method to establish new identities among Bernoulli, harmonic, and Stirling numbers.
result: Several new identities relating Bernoulli numbers, harmonic numbers, and Stirling numbers are presented.
conclusion: The results contribute to classical combinatorial number theory and may be useful for further identity derivations, but have no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Formalising John Dee's Monas Hieroglyphica In Lean 4
authors: Ivan Matychyn
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: John Dee's Monas Hieroglyphica (Antwerp, 1564) contains twenty-four numbered theorems about a single composite alchemical glyph, presented in the manner of Euclid: theorem, demonstration, corollary. In this note the following question is considered: which of Dee's theorems can be stated precisely in a proof assistant, and which of them can then be proved? Working in Lean 4 (v4.35.0) with the core library only (without Mathlib), we divide the treatise into three layers: the syntax of the glyph, encoded as inductive data; Dee's arithmetic, verified by kernel computation; and the geometry of the final theorems, in connection with which we prove a classical result not stated by Dee: no ratio of whole numbers doubles the cube, that is, the cube root of two is irrational (the Delian obstruction). The accompanying file Monas.lean compiles with no errors and no sorry. Two observations are made. The cabalistic computation of Theorem XVII, according to which the Cross, "by the best kabbalistic computation," signifies the number 252, is verified, and its proof depends on no axioms: it is a pure computation. The only theorem of the formalisation with genuine mathematical content, the Delian obstruction, is proved constructively and depends only on the axioms propext and Quot.sound.
tags: irrationality of cube root of two
tldr: A short note formalising John Dee's 1564 alchemical treatise Monas Hieroglyphica in Lean 4, separating glyph syntax, Dee's arithmetic, and the geometry of the closing theorems.
motivation: The author asks which of Dee's twenty-four Euclidean-style theorems can be stated and proved precisely in a modern proof assistant, treating a Renaissance esoteric text as a formalisation exercise.
method: The treatise is encoded in Lean 4 (v4.35.0) using only the core library, with the glyph as inductive data, arithmetic checked by kernel computation, and geometry handled separately; the accompanying Monas.lean file compiles without sorry.
result: Theorem XVII's cabalistic computation of 252 is verified axiom-free as pure computation, while the sole theorem with genuine mathematical content — the irrationality of the cube root of two (Delian obstruction) — is proved constructively from propext and Quot.sound.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a layered formalisation of a historical alchemical text, showing most of Dee's theorems lack provable mathematical substance beyond one classical irrationality result.
keywords: irrationality of cube root of two

title: Sharp Bounds On Continuous Treatment Effects Under Unobserved Confounding
authors: Junzhe Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study partial identification of conditional treatment effects with a continuous treatment under unobserved confounding. We target the conditional average potential outcome (CAPO) E[Y_x|z] and the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) between two treatment levels. We assume a bounded outcome and Lipschitz continuity of the response functions and of the propensity scores given the latent confounder, and show that these conditions imply the smooth treatment response and smooth treatment selection conditions of Kim et al. (2018). The combined bound of Kim et al. uses only two reference points on the identified diagonal and is generally loose. Bounding through every diagonal reference point instead gives explicit bounds whose average is the sharp identified set of the CAPO at every treatment, inside or outside the observational support. Capping the difference between the upper and lower bounds gives sharp causal bounds on the CATE. These bounds are informative without monotonicity or overlap assumptions.
tldr: The paper derives sharp partial-identification bounds for conditional average potential outcomes and treatment effects with continuous treatments under unobserved confounding.
motivation: Standard causal bounds with continuous treatments and hidden confounders (e.g., the Kim et al. combined bound) rely on only two diagonal reference points and are typically loose, so tighter sharp bounds are needed.
method: Assuming bounded outcomes plus Lipschitz continuity of response functions and propensity scores in the latent confounder, the authors bound the CAPO through every diagonal reference point and average these to obtain an explicit sharp identified set, then difference upper and lower bounds to bound the CATE.
result: The averaged bounds yield the sharp identified set of the CAPO at every treatment level, including outside the observational support, and produce informative CATE bounds without monotonicity or overlap assumptions.
conclusion: The proposed Lipschitz-based construction gives sharper, assumption-light causal bounds for continuous treatments, improving on existing two-reference-point approaches.

title: Blind Random Search With Noisy Measurements: Almost Sure Convergence And Convergence Rates
authors: James C. Spall Zixian Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2610.33302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Blind random search is a simple global optimization method that only requires the value of the loss function, without needing gradient information or an explicit loss model. However, its classical formulation assumes that the loss evaluation is noise-free, which limits its direct application to practical problems with noisy measurements. We extend blind random search by combining a vanishing acceptance threshold with the running average of noisy loss measurements. Under the stated assumptions, we prove that the proposed algorithm converges almost surely to the global minimizer. We further analyze the rate at which the loss at the current estimate approaches the minimum loss. For low-dimensional cases, we obtain an almost sure asymptotic upper bound on the difference between the two, and for high-dimensional cases, we prove that this difference, suitably scaled, has an exact Weibull limiting distribution.
tldr: The paper extends blind random search to settings with noisy loss evaluations and establishes almost-sure convergence to the global minimizer along with convergence-rate guarantees.
motivation: Classical blind random search assumes noise-free loss evaluations, which severely limits its applicability to real-world optimization problems where measurements are noisy.
method: The authors combine a vanishing acceptance threshold with a running average of noisy loss measurements, then analyze the resulting stochastic algorithm under stated assumptions.
result: They prove almost-sure convergence to the global minimizer, derive an almost-sure asymptotic upper bound on the optimality gap in low dimensions, and show that in high dimensions the suitably scaled gap follows an exact Weibull limiting distribution.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous convergence and rate theory for noisy blind random search, making the method viable for practical stochastic optimization.

title: Protect The Decision, Not The Disaster: Regret-Robust Capacity Sizing And Positioning With Transportation Recourse
authors: Elioth Sanabria
